The **2024 NBA draft** was the 78th edition of the [National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association")'s annual [draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_draft "NBA draft"). Unlike recent years, the 2024 draft took place over two nights. This was the first NBA draft held over multiple nights since the current two-round format debuted in [1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_NBA_draft "1989 NBA draft").

The first round of the draft took place on June 26, 2024, at [Barclays Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays_Center "Barclays Center") in [Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn "Brooklyn"), New York, while the second round took place on June 27 at [ESPN's Seaport District Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Street_Seaport#ESPN_studios "South Street Seaport") in [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan"). The time between second-round picks expanded from two minutes to four.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-2) For the third year in a row, the draft had 58 picks instead of the typical 60: both the [Philadelphia 76ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers") and the [Phoenix Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Suns "Phoenix Suns") lost second-round picks for violations of the NBA's [tampering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tapping_up "Tapping up") rules during free agency.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-76ersTamper-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-SunsTamper-4)

The [first overall selection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_first_overall_NBA_draft_picks "List of first overall NBA draft picks") was owned by the [Atlanta Hawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Hawks "Atlanta Hawks"), which they used to select French forward [Zaccharie Risacher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zaccharie_Risacher "Zaccharie Risacher"), making him the second consecutive French player to be drafted with the number one pick, after the [San Antonio Spurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Antonio_Spurs "San Antonio Spurs") had picked [Victor Wembanyama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama "Victor Wembanyama") in the [previous year's edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NBA_draft "2023 NBA draft").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-:0-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-:1-7) France became the second nation (after the U.S.) to have at least three native players picked in the top 10 spots of any NBA draft following the selections of Risacher, [Alex Sarr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Sarr "Alex Sarr"), and [Tidjane Salaün](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tidjane_Sala%C3%BCn "Tidjane Salaün"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-:0-5)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-:1-7) as well as the second nation (after the U.S.) to have two native players get selected with the first and second overall picks.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-:1-7) The eventual [Rookie of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Rookie_of_the_Year "NBA Rookie of the Year") would be fourth pick [Stephon Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephon_Castle "Stephon Castle") for the Spurs.

[Bronny James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronny_James "Bronny James"), the son of [LeBron James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeBron_James "LeBron James"), was selected 55th overall in the second round and would become the first player in NBA history to play alongside his father.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-8)

The **2024 NBA draft** was the 78th edition of the [National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association")'s annual [draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_draft "NBA draft"). Unlike recent years, the 2024 draft took place over two nights. This was the first NBA draft held over multiple nights since the current two-round format debuted in [1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_NBA_draft "1989 NBA draft").

The first round of the draft took place on June 26, 2024, at [Barclays Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays_Center "Barclays Center") in [Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn "Brooklyn"), New York, while the second round took place on June 27 at [ESPN's Seaport District Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Street_Seaport#ESPN_studios "South Street Seaport") in [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan"). The time between second-round picks expanded from two minutes to four.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-2) For the third year in a row, the draft had 58 picks instead of the typical 60: both the [Philadelphia 76ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers") and the [Phoenix Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Suns "Phoenix Suns") lost second-round picks for violations of the NBA's [tampering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tapping_up "Tapping up") rules during free agency.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-76ersTamper-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-SunsTamper-4)

The [first overall selection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_first_overall_NBA_draft_picks "List of first overall NBA draft picks") was owned by the [Atlanta Hawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Hawks "Atlanta Hawks"), which they used to select French forward [Zaccharie Risacher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zaccharie_Risacher "Zaccharie Risacher"), making him the second consecutive French player to be drafted with the number one pick, after the [San Antonio Spurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Antonio_Spurs "San Antonio Spurs") had picked [Victor Wembanyama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Wembanyama "Victor Wembanyama") in the [previous year's edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NBA_draft "2023 NBA draft").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-:0-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-:1-7) France became the second nation (after the U.S.) to have at least three native players picked in the top 10 spots of any NBA draft following the selections of Risacher, [Alex Sarr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Sarr "Alex Sarr"), and [Tidjane Salaün](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tidjane_Sala%C3%BCn "Tidjane Salaün"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-:0-5)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-:1-7) as well as the second nation (after the U.S.) to have two native players get selected with the first and second overall picks.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-:1-7) The eventual [Rookie of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Rookie_of_the_Year "NBA Rookie of the Year") would be fourth pick [Stephon Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephon_Castle "Stephon Castle") for the Spurs.

[Bronny James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronny_James "Bronny James"), the son of [LeBron James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeBron_James "LeBron James"), was selected 55th overall in the second round and would become the first player in NBA history to play alongside his father.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_draft#cite_note-8)

The **2021 NBA draft**, the 75th edition of the [National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association")'s annual [draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_draft "NBA draft"), was held on July 29, 2021, at [Barclays Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays_Center "Barclays Center") in [Brooklyn, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn "Brooklyn"). The NBA draft returned to Brooklyn after [the previous year's draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NBA_draft "2020 NBA draft") was held through [videoconferencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Videoconferencing "Videoconferencing") at [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN") Studios in [Bristol, Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bristol,_Connecticut "Bristol, Connecticut") due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"). With the first overall pick, the [Detroit Pistons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Pistons "Detroit Pistons") selected [Cade Cunningham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cade_Cunningham "Cade Cunningham").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_NBA_draft#cite_note-2) The NBA used a "ceremonial pick" for the late [Terrence Clarke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrence_Clarke "Terrence Clarke"), between the 14th and 15th pick of the draft.

Prior to the draft, the following trades were made and resulted in exchanges of draft picks between teams.

1.   12February 6, 2020: [Minnesota Timberwolves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Timberwolves "Minnesota Timberwolves") to [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_State_Warriors "Golden State Warriors")[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_NBA_draft#cite_note-4)
    *   Golden State acquired [Andrew Wiggins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Wiggins "Andrew Wiggins"), a _top-3 protected 2021 first-round pick_, and a _second-round draft pick_

The **2021 NBA draft**, the 75th edition of the [National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association")'s annual [draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_draft "NBA draft"), was held on July 29, 2021, at [Barclays Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays_Center "Barclays Center") in [Brooklyn, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn "Brooklyn"). The NBA draft returned to Brooklyn after [the previous year's draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NBA_draft "2020 NBA draft") was held through [videoconferencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Videoconferencing "Videoconferencing") at [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN") Studios in [Bristol, Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bristol,_Connecticut "Bristol, Connecticut") due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"). With the first overall pick, the [Detroit Pistons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Pistons "Detroit Pistons") selected [Cade Cunningham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cade_Cunningham "Cade Cunningham").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_NBA_draft#cite_note-2) The NBA used a "ceremonial pick" for the late [Terrence Clarke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrence_Clarke "Terrence Clarke"), between the 14th and 15th pick of the draft.

## Trades involving draft picks

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2021_NBA_draft&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Trades involving draft picks")]

### Pre-draft trades

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2021_NBA_draft&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Pre-draft trades")]

Prior to the draft, the following trades were made and resulted in exchanges of draft picks between teams.

1.   12February 6, 2020: [Minnesota Timberwolves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Timberwolves "Minnesota Timberwolves") to [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_State_Warriors "Golden State Warriors")[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_NBA_draft#cite_note-4)
    *   Golden State acquired [Andrew Wiggins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Wiggins "Andrew Wiggins"), a _top-3 protected 2021 first-round pick_, and a _second-round draft pick_
    *   Minnesota acquired [D'Angelo Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Angelo_Russell "D'Angelo Russell"), [Jacob Evans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Evans "Jacob Evans"), and [Omari Spellman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omari_Spellman "Omari Spellman")

2.   ↑March 25, 2021: [Chicago Bulls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bulls "Chicago Bulls") to [Orlando Magic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic "Orlando Magic")[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_NBA_draft#cite_note-6)
    *   Orlando acquired [Wendell Carter Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendell_Carter_Jr. "Wendell Carter Jr."), [Otto Porter Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otto_Porter_Jr. "Otto Porter Jr."), _2021_ and 2023 first-round picks
    *   Chicago acquired [Nikola Vučević](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikola_Vu%C4%8Devi%C4%87 "Nikola Vučević"), and [Al-Farouq Aminu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Farouq_Aminu "Al-Farouq Aminu")

3.   ↑June 18, 2021: [Boston Celtics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Celtics "Boston Celtics") to [Oklahoma City Thunder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma_City_Thunder "Oklahoma City Thunder")[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_NBA_draft#cite_note-11)
    *   Oklahoma City acquired [Kemba Walker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kemba_Walker "Kemba Walker"), a _2021 first-round pick_, and 2025 second-round picks
    *   Boston acquired [Al Horford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Horford "Al Horford"), [Moses Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moses_Brown_(basketball) "Moses Brown (basketball)"), and a 2023 second-round pick

4.   ↑February 19, 2015: [Miami Heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Heat "Miami Heat") to [Phoenix Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Suns "Phoenix Suns") (three-team trade with [New Orleans Pelicans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Pelicans "New Orleans Pelicans"))[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_NBA_draft#cite_note-15)
    *   Phoenix acquired [Danny Granger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Granger "Danny Granger"), [John Salmons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Salmons "John Salmons"), a _2021 first-round pick_, and a 2017 protected first-round pick
    *   Miami acquired [Goran Dragić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goran_Dragi%C4%87 "Goran Dragić") and [Zoran Dragić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoran_Dragi%C4%87 "Zoran Dragić")
    *   New Orleans acquired [Norris Cole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norris_Cole "Norris Cole"), [Justin Hamilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Hamilton_(basketball,_born_1990) "Justin Hamilton (basketball, born 1990)") and [Shawne Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawne_Williams "Shawne Williams")

 June 21, 2018: [Phoenix Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Suns "Phoenix Suns") to [Philadelphia 76ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers")[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_NBA_draft#cite_note-16)
    *   Philadelphia acquired [Zhaire Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhaire_Smith "Zhaire Smith") and _Miami's 2021 first-round pick_
    *   Phoenix acquired [Mikal Bridges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikal_Bridges "Mikal Bridges")

5.   12February 6, 2019: [Philadelphia 76ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers") to [Los Angeles Clippers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Clippers "Los Angeles Clippers")[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_NBA_draft#cite_note-18)
    *   L.A. The **2015 NBA draft** was held on June 25, 2015, at [Barclays Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays_Center "Barclays Center") in [Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn "Brooklyn"). It was televised nationally in the U.S. by ESPN. [National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") (NBA) teams took turns selecting amateur U.S. [college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") players and other eligible players, including international players. The [draft lottery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_draft_lottery "NBA draft lottery") took place on May 19, 2015.

The [Minnesota Timberwolves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Timberwolves "Minnesota Timberwolves") won the [draft lottery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_draft_lottery "NBA draft lottery") to earn the [first overall pick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_first_overall_NBA_draft_picks "List of first overall NBA draft picks") in the draft. It marked the first time in Timberwolves history that they would receive the first overall pick through the lottery. The player selected would also be the third consecutive number one pick on the Timberwolves roster, joining [Andrew Wiggins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Wiggins "Andrew Wiggins") (2014) and [Anthony Bennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Bennett_(basketball) "Anthony Bennett (basketball)") (2013) - who were traded to Minnesota for forward [Kevin Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Love "Kevin Love"). This draft also gave the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers") the second overall pick after jumping over the [Philadelphia 76ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers") and the [New York Knicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Knicks "New York Knicks") within the draft lottery.

Highlights from the draft include the first Dominican to be the first overall pick ([Karl-Anthony Towns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns "Karl-Anthony Towns")), the highest number of Kentucky Wildcats selected in the draft lottery (four with Karl-Anthony Towns, [Willie Cauley-Stein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Cauley-Stein "Willie Cauley-Stein"), [Trey Lyles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trey_Lyles "Trey Lyles"), and [Devin Booker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Booker "Devin Booker")), which tied the [North Carolina Tar Heels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina_Tar_Heels_men's_basketball "North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball") in 2005 for most players selected in the lottery by one school; the tied record for most Kentucky players selected in the draft (six with Towns, Cauley-Stein, Lyles, Booker, [Andrew Harrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Harrison_(basketball) "Andrew Harrison (basketball)"), and [Dakari Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dakari_Johnson "Dakari Johnson")), the second Latvian to have been drafted in the first round ([Kristaps Porziņģis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristaps_Porzi%C5%86%C4%A3is "Kristaps Porziņģis")), the first former high school player to have skipped college to play in China that was selected in the draft ([Emmanuel Mudiay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmanuel_Mudiay "Emmanuel Mudiay")), and the first Indian-born player to have been selected in the NBA ([Satnam Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satnam_Singh "Satnam Singh")),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-1) who was also the first player since 2005 to have been drafted directly from high school (albeit as a [postgraduate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postgraduate_year "Postgraduate year")).

Other noteworthy announcements that came out of the draft included the official announcement of the passing of the last pioneer of the original NBA, [Harvey Pollack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvey_Pollack "Harvey Pollack"), around the third pick and the resignation of the league's president of basketball operations [Rod Thorn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rod_Thorn "Rod Thorn") that became official in August after the end of the first round.

## Eligibility and entrants

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_NBA_draft&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Eligibility and entrants")]

Main article: [Eligibility for the NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eligibility_for_the_NBA_draft "Eligibility for the NBA draft")

The draft was conducted under the eligibility rules established in the league's new 2011 [collective bargaining agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Collective_Bargaining_Agreement "NBA Collective Bargaining Agreement") (CBA) with its players union. The CBA that ended the [2011 lockout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_NBA_lockout "2011 NBA lockout") instituted no immediate changes to the draft, but called for a committee of owners and players to discuss future changes.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-2011_status_quo-96) Since the 2011 CBA, the basic eligibility rules have been:

*   All drafted players must be at least 19 years old during the calendar year of the draft. In terms of dates, players eligible for the 2015 draft must be born on or before December 31, 1996.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-CBA_Age-97)
*   Any player who is not an "international player", as defined in the CBA, must be at least one year removed from the graduation of his high school class.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-CBA_Age-97) The CBA defines "international players" as players who permanently resided outside the United States for three years prior to the draft, did not complete high school in the U.S., and have never enrolled at a U.S. college or university.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-CBA_International-98)

### Early entrants

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_NBA_draft&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Early entrants")]

Player who are not automatically eligible must declare their eligibility for the draft by notifying the NBA offices in writing no later than 60 days before the draft.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-CBA_US_Early_Entry-99)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-CBA_International_Early_Entry-100) For the 2015 draft, this date fell on April 26. After this date, "early entry" players may attend NBA pre-draft camps and individual team workouts to show off their skills and obtain feedback regarding their draft positions. Under the CBA, a player may withdraw his name from consideration from the draft at any time before the final declaration date, which is 10 days before the draft.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-CBA_Withdrawal-101) Under NCAA rules at that time, players only had until April 16 to withdraw from the draft and maintain their college eligibility.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-NCAA_withdrawal-102) In January 2016, the NCAA changed its draft withdrawal date to 10 days after the end of the annual [NBA Draft Combine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Draft_Combine "NBA Draft Combine") in May, with the [2016 draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_NBA_draft "2016 NBA draft") the first to be held under the new rule.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-Goodman_2016-01-13-103)

A player who has hired an [agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_agent "Sports agent") will forfeit his remaining college eligibility, regardless of whether he is drafted.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-NCAA_agent-104) Also, while the CBA allows a player to withdraw from the draft twice,[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-CBA_Withdrawal-101) the NCAA then mandated that a player who declared twice lost his college eligibility.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-NCAA_withdrawal-102) The aforementioned 2016 NCAA rule change also allowed players to declare for more than one draft without losing college eligibility.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-Goodman_2016-01-13-103)

This year, a total of 48 collegiate players and 43 international players declared as early entry candidates before the April 26 deadline.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-earlyentrant-105) On June 15, the withdrawal deadline, 34 early entry candidates withdrew from the draft and one early entry candidate is added, leaving 47 collegiate players and 11 international players as the early entry candidates for the draft.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-earlyentrantwithdraw-106)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-earlyentrantlist-107)

The **2015 NBA draft** was held on June 25, 2015, at [Barclays Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays_Center "Barclays Center") in [Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn "Brooklyn"). It was televised nationally in the U.S. by ESPN. [National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") (NBA) teams took turns selecting amateur U.S. [college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") players and other eligible players, including international players. The [draft lottery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_draft_lottery "NBA draft lottery") took place on May 19, 2015.

The [Minnesota Timberwolves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Timberwolves "Minnesota Timberwolves") won the [draft lottery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_draft_lottery "NBA draft lottery") to earn the [first overall pick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_first_overall_NBA_draft_picks "List of first overall NBA draft picks") in the draft. It marked the first time in Timberwolves history that they would receive the first overall pick through the lottery. The player selected would also be the third consecutive number one pick on the Timberwolves roster, joining [Andrew Wiggins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Wiggins "Andrew Wiggins") (2014) and [Anthony Bennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Bennett_(basketball) "Anthony Bennett (basketball)") (2013) - who were traded to Minnesota for forward [Kevin Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Love "Kevin Love"). This draft also gave the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers") the second overall pick after jumping over the [Philadelphia 76ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers") and the [New York Knicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Knicks "New York Knicks") within the draft lottery.

Highlights from the draft include the first Dominican to be the first overall pick ([Karl-Anthony Towns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns "Karl-Anthony Towns")), the highest number of Kentucky Wildcats selected in the draft lottery (four with Karl-Anthony Towns, [Willie Cauley-Stein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Cauley-Stein "Willie Cauley-Stein"), [Trey Lyles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trey_Lyles "Trey Lyles"), and [Devin Booker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Booker "Devin Booker")), which tied the [North Carolina Tar Heels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina_Tar_Heels_men's_basketball "North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball") in 2005 for most players selected in the lottery by one school; the tied record for most Kentucky players selected in the draft (six with Towns, Cauley-Stein, Lyles, Booker, [Andrew Harrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Harrison_(basketball) "Andrew Harrison (basketball)"), and [Dakari Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dakari_Johnson "Dakari Johnson")), the second Latvian to have been drafted in the first round ([Kristaps Porziņģis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristaps_Porzi%C5%86%C4%A3is "Kristaps Porziņģis")), the first former high school player to have skipped college to play in China that was selected in the draft ([Emmanuel Mudiay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmanuel_Mudiay "Emmanuel Mudiay")), and the first Indian-born player to have been selected in the NBA ([Satnam Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satnam_Singh "Satnam Singh")),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-1) who was also the first player since 2005 to have been drafted directly from high school (albeit as a [postgraduate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postgraduate_year "Postgraduate year")).

Other noteworthy announcements that came out of the draft included the official announcement of the passing of the last pioneer of the original NBA, [Harvey Pollack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvey_Pollack "Harvey Pollack"), around the third pick and the resignation of the league's president of basketball operations [Rod Thorn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rod_Thorn "Rod Thorn") that became official in August after the end of the first round.

## Eligibility and entrants

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_NBA_draft&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Eligibility and entrants")]

Main article: [Eligibility for the NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eligibility_for_the_NBA_draft "Eligibility for the NBA draft")

The draft was conducted under the eligibility rules established in the league's new 2011 [collective bargaining agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Collective_Bargaining_Agreement "NBA Collective Bargaining Agreement") (CBA) with its players union. The CBA that ended the [2011 lockout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_NBA_lockout "2011 NBA lockout") instituted no immediate changes to the draft, but called for a committee of owners and players to discuss future changes.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-2011_status_quo-96) Since the 2011 CBA, the basic eligibility rules have been:

*   All drafted players must be at least 19 years old during the calendar year of the draft. In terms of dates, players eligible for the 2015 draft must be born on or before December 31, 1996.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-CBA_Age-97)
*   Any player who is not an "international player", as defined in the CBA, must be at least one year removed from the graduation of his high school class.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-CBA_Age-97) The CBA defines "international players" as players who permanently resided outside the United States for three years prior to the draft, did not complete high school in the U.S., and have never enrolled at a U.S. college or university.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-CBA_International-98)

### Early entrants

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_NBA_draft&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Early entrants")]

Player who are not automatically eligible must declare their eligibility for the draft by notifying the NBA offices in writing no later than 60 days before the draft.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-CBA_US_Early_Entry-99)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-CBA_International_Early_Entry-100) For the 2015 draft, this date fell on April 26. After this date, "early entry" players may attend NBA pre-draft camps and individual team workouts to show off their skills and obtain feedback regarding their draft positions. Under the CBA, a player may withdraw his name from consideration from the draft at any time before the final declaration date, which is 10 days before the draft.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-CBA_Withdrawal-101) Under NCAA rules at that time, players only had until April 16 to withdraw from the draft and maintain their college eligibility.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-NCAA_withdrawal-102) In January 2016, the NCAA changed its draft withdrawal date to 10 days after the end of the annual [NBA Draft Combine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Draft_Combine "NBA Draft Combine") in May, with the [2016 draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_NBA_draft "2016 NBA draft") the first to be held under the new rule.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-Goodman_2016-01-13-103)

A player who has hired an [agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_agent "Sports agent") will forfeit his remaining college eligibility, regardless of whether he is drafted.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-NCAA_agent-104) Also, while the CBA allows a player to withdraw from the draft twice,[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-CBA_Withdrawal-101) the NCAA then mandated that a player who declared twice lost his college eligibility.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-NCAA_withdrawal-102) The aforementioned 2016 NCAA rule change also allowed players to declare for more than one draft without losing college eligibility.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-Goodman_2016-01-13-103)

This year, a total of 48 collegiate players and 43 international players declared as early entry candidates before the April 26 deadline.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-earlyentrant-105) On June 15, the withdrawal deadline, 34 early entry candidates withdrew from the draft and one early entry candidate is added, leaving 47 collegiate players and 11 international players as the early entry candidates for the draft.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-earlyentrantwithdraw-106)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-earlyentrantlist-107)

The **2015 NBA draft** was held on June 25, 2015, at [Barclays Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays_Center "Barclays Center") in [Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn "Brooklyn"). It was televised nationally in the U.S. by ESPN. [National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") (NBA) teams took turns selecting amateur U.S. [college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") players and other eligible players, including international players. The [draft lottery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_draft_lottery "NBA draft lottery") took place on May 19, 2015.

The [Minnesota Timberwolves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Timberwolves "Minnesota Timberwolves") won the [draft lottery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_draft_lottery "NBA draft lottery") to earn the [first overall pick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_first_overall_NBA_draft_picks "List of first overall NBA draft picks") in the draft. It marked the first time in Timberwolves history that they would receive the first overall pick through the lottery. The player selected would also be the third consecutive number one pick on the Timberwolves roster, joining [Andrew Wiggins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Wiggins "Andrew Wiggins") (2014) and [Anthony Bennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Bennett_(basketball) "Anthony Bennett (basketball)") (2013) - who were traded to Minnesota for forward [Kevin Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Love "Kevin Love"). This draft also gave the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers") the second overall pick after jumping over the [Philadelphia 76ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers") and the [New York Knicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Knicks "New York Knicks") within the draft lottery.

Highlights from the draft include the first Dominican to be the first overall pick ([Karl-Anthony Towns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns "Karl-Anthony Towns")), the highest number of Kentucky Wildcats selected in the draft lottery (four with Karl-Anthony Towns, [Willie Cauley-Stein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Cauley-Stein "Willie Cauley-Stein"), [Trey Lyles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trey_Lyles "Trey Lyles"), and [Devin Booker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Booker "Devin Booker")), which tied the [North Carolina Tar Heels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina_Tar_Heels_men's_basketball "North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball") in 2005 for most players selected in the lottery by one school; the tied record for most Kentucky players selected in the draft (six with Towns, Cauley-Stein, Lyles, Booker, [Andrew Harrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Harrison_(basketball) "Andrew Harrison (basketball)"), and [Dakari Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dakari_Johnson "Dakari Johnson")), the second Latvian to have been drafted in the first round ([Kristaps Porziņģis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristaps_Porzi%C5%86%C4%A3is "Kristaps Porziņģis")), the first former high school player to have skipped college to play in China that was selected in the draft ([Emmanuel Mudiay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmanuel_Mudiay "Emmanuel Mudiay")), and the first Indian-born player to have been selected in the NBA ([Satnam Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satnam_Singh "Satnam Singh")),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-1) who was also the first player since 2005 to have been drafted directly from high school (albeit as a [postgraduate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postgraduate_year "Postgraduate year")).

Other noteworthy announcements that came out of the draft included the official announcement of the passing of the last pioneer of the original NBA, [Harvey Pollack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvey_Pollack "Harvey Pollack"), around the third pick and the resignation of the league's president of basketball operations [Rod Thorn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rod_Thorn "Rod Thorn") that became official in August after the end of the first round.

## Eligibility and entrants

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_NBA_draft&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Eligibility and entrants")]

Main article: [Eligibility for the NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eligibility_for_the_NBA_draft "Eligibility for the NBA draft")

The draft was conducted under the eligibility rules established in the league's new 2011 [collective bargaining agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Collective_Bargaining_Agreement "NBA Collective Bargaining Agreement") (CBA) with its players union. The CBA that ended the [2011 lockout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_NBA_lockout "2011 NBA lockout") instituted no immediate changes to the draft, but called for a committee of owners and players to discuss future changes.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-2011_status_quo-96) Since the 2011 CBA, the basic eligibility rules have been:

*   All drafted players must be at least 19 years old during the calendar year of the draft. In terms of dates, players eligible for the 2015 draft must be born on or before December 31, 1996.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-CBA_Age-97)
*   Any player who is not an "international player", as defined in the CBA, must be at least one year removed from the graduation of his high school class.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-CBA_Age-97) The CBA defines "international players" as players who permanently resided outside the United States for three years prior to the draft, did not complete high school in the U.S., and have never enrolled at a U.S. college or university.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-CBA_International-98)

### Early entrants

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2015_NBA_draft&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Early entrants")]

Player who are not automatically eligible must declare their eligibility for the draft by notifying the NBA offices in writing no later than 60 days before the draft.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-CBA_US_Early_Entry-99)[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-CBA_International_Early_Entry-100) For the 2015 draft, this date fell on April 26. After this date, "early entry" players may attend NBA pre-draft camps and individual team workouts to show off their skills and obtain feedback regarding their draft positions. Under the CBA, a player may withdraw his name from consideration from the draft at any time before the final declaration date, which is 10 days before the draft.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-CBA_Withdrawal-101) Under NCAA rules at that time, players only had until April 16 to withdraw from the draft and maintain their college eligibility.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-NCAA_withdrawal-102) In January 2016, the NCAA changed its draft withdrawal date to 10 days after the end of the annual [NBA Draft Combine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Draft_Combine "NBA Draft Combine") in May, with the [2016 draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_NBA_draft "2016 NBA draft") the first to be held under the new rule.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-Goodman_2016-01-13-103)

A player who has hired an [agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_agent "Sports agent") will forfeit his remaining college eligibility, regardless of whether he is drafted.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-NCAA_agent-104) Also, while the CBA allows a player to withdraw from the draft twice,[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-CBA_Withdrawal-101) the NCAA then mandated that a player who declared twice lost his college eligibility.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-NCAA_withdrawal-102) The aforementioned 2016 NCAA rule change also allowed players to declare for more than one draft without losing college eligibility.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-Goodman_2016-01-13-103)

This year, a total of 48 collegiate players and 43 international players declared as early entry candidates before the April 26 deadline.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-earlyentrant-105) On June 15, the withdrawal deadline, 34 early entry candidates withdrew from the draft and one early entry candidate is added, leaving 47 collegiate players and 11 international players as the early entry candidates for the draft.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-earlyentrantwithdraw-106)[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_draft#cite_note-earlyentrantlist-107)

The **2016 NBA draft** was held on June 23, 2016, at [Barclays Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays_Center "Barclays Center") in [Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn "Brooklyn"). It was televised nationally in the U.S. by [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_on_ESPN "NBA on ESPN"), and was [live streamed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_streaming "Live streaming") for the first time in NBA draft history by [The Vertical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yahoo!_Sports "Yahoo! Sports").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_NBA_draft#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_NBA_draft#cite_note-2)[National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") (NBA) teams took turns selecting amateur U.S. [college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") players and other eligible players, including international players. The [draft lottery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_draft_lottery "NBA draft lottery") took place during the playoffs, on May 17, 2016. This was the first time since the lottery system was introduced in 1985 that all NBA teams that missed out on the playoffs remained in the exact spots they were designated, meaning the 10-win/72-loss Philadelphia 76ers received the No. 1 pick, the Los Angeles Lakers kept the No. 2 pick, the Boston Celtics via the Brooklyn Nets got the No. 3 pick, and everyone else stayed in their same spots based on the regular season standings from the [2015–16 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_NBA_season "2015–16 NBA season").

Highlights from the draft include the second Australian No. 1 draft pick ([Ben Simmons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Simmons "Ben Simmons"); the first being [Andrew Bogut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Bogut "Andrew Bogut")), the first Austrian to be selected into the NBA ([Jakob Pöltl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jakob_P%C3%B6ltl "Jakob Pöltl")), the first [Ghanaian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana") to be selected into the NBA ([Ben Bentil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Bentil "Ben Bentil")), the most Frenchmen to be taken overall ([Guerschon Yabusele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guerschon_Yabusele "Guerschon Yabusele"), [Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timoth%C3%A9_Luwawu-Cabarrot "Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot"), [David Michineau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Michineau "David Michineau"), [Isaia Cordinier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaia_Cordinier "Isaia Cordinier"), [Petr Cornelie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petr_Cornelie "Petr Cornelie")), the first time since the [1990 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_NBA_draft "1990 NBA draft") that an [Egyptian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt "Egypt") has been selected into the NBA ([Abdel Nader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdel_Nader "Abdel Nader")), and the first time that two [Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China") players have been selected into the same draft ([Zhou Qi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhou_Qi "Zhou Qi") and [Wang Zhelin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Zhelin "Wang Zhelin")) since the [2007 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_NBA_draft "2007 NBA draft"). This draft was also notable for providing the most international draft prospects in draft history, with 28 different players representing different countries instead of the United States of America. It beat out the [2004 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_NBA_draft "2004 NBA draft") for the most culturally diverse draft in league history. It was the second time that three players were selected from [Serbian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbia "Serbia") team [Mega Leks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KK_Mega_Basket "KK Mega Basket") in the same draft ([Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timoth%C3%A9_Luwawu-Cabarrot "Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot"), [Ivica Zubac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivica_Zubac "Ivica Zubac"), [Rade Zagorac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rade_Zagorac "Rade Zagorac")), the first time being the [2014 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_NBA_draft "2014 NBA draft").

## Eligibility and entrants

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_NBA_draft&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Eligibility and entrants")]

Main article: [Eligibility for the NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eligibility_for_the_NBA_draft "Eligibility for the NBA draft")

The draft is conducted under the eligibility rules established in the league's 2011 [collective bargaining agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Collective_Bargaining_Agreement "NBA Collective Bargaining Agreement") (CBA) with its players union. The CBA that ended the [2011 lockout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_NBA_lockout "2011 NBA lockout") instituted no immediate changes to the draft, but called for a committee of owners and players to discuss future changes.

*   All drafted players must be at least 19 years old during the calendar year of the draft. In terms of dates, players, who are eligible for the 2016 draft, must be born on or before December 31, 1997.
*   On January 13, 2016, the [NCAA Division I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_I "NCAA Division I") council approved a new rule for that division that significantly changed the draft landscape for college players:[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_NBA_draft#cite_note-91)
    *   Declaration for the draft no longer results in automatic loss of college eligibility. As long as a player does not sign a contract with a professional team outside the NBA, or sign with an agent, he will retain college eligibility as long as he makes a timely withdrawal from the draft.
    *   NCAA players now have until 10 days after the end of the [NBA Draft Combine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Draft_Combine "NBA Draft Combine") to withdraw from the draft. For 2016, the withdrawal date was May 25, about five weeks after the previous mid-April deadline.
    *   NCAA players may participate in the draft combine, and will also be allowed to attend one tryout per year with each NBA team without losing college eligibility.
    *   NCAA players may now enter and withdraw from the draft multiple times without loss of eligibility. Previously, the NCAA treated a second declaration of draft eligibility as a permanent loss of college eligibility.

The NBA has since expanded the draft combine to include players with remaining college eligibility (who, like players without college eligibility, can only attend by invitation).[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_NBA_draft#cite_note-92)

### Early entrants

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_NBA_draft&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Early entrants")]

Player who are not automatically eligible must declare their eligibility for the draft by notifying the NBA offices in writing no later than 60 days before the draft. For the 2016 draft, this date fell on April 24. After this date "early entry" players may attend NBA pre-draft camps and individual team workouts to show off their skills and obtain feedback regarding their draft positions. Under the CBA a player may withdraw his name from consideration from the draft at any time before the final declaration date, which is 10 days before the draft. Under newly implemented NCAA rules, players had until May 25 (10 days after the draft combine) to withdraw from the draft and retain college eligibility.

A player who has hired an agent will forfeit his remaining college eligibility regardless of whether he is drafted. The CBA allows a player to withdraw from the draft twice; the 2016 NCAA rule change brought it in line with the CBA on this detail.

#### College underclassmen

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_NBA_draft&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: College underclassmen")]

A record-high 162 under-classed draft prospects had declared themselves for eligibility at the April 24 deadline (116 of them being from college), although college players who had not hired agents or signed professional contracts outside the NBA were able to decide to return to college by May 25, 10 days after the end of the [NBA Draft Combine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Draft_Combine "NBA Draft Combine").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_NBA_draft#cite_note-93) At the end of the May 25 deadline, there were 57 players confirming their intentions of returning to school, thus leaving the grand total of underclassmen participating in the NBA draft as 59. Players listed in this region have publicly indicated that they have hired agents, planned to do so around this time, or made themselves their own agents; those who have hired agents and weren't drafted are deemed ineligible to return to NCAA basketball in 2016–17. However, with this year's draft class, it provided the most undrafted college underclassmen out there with 30 people there not being taken at all.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_NBA_draft#cite_note-94)

The **2016 NBA draft** was held on June 23, 2016, at [Barclays Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barclays_Center "Barclays Center") in [Brooklyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn "Brooklyn"). It was televised nationally in the U.S. by [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_on_ESPN "NBA on ESPN"), and was [live streamed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_streaming "Live streaming") for the first time in NBA draft history by [The Vertical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yahoo!_Sports "Yahoo! Sports").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_NBA_draft#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_NBA_draft#cite_note-2)[National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") (NBA) teams took turns selecting amateur U.S. [college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") players and other eligible players, including international players. The [draft lottery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_draft_lottery "NBA draft lottery") took place during the playoffs, on May 17, 2016. This was the first time since the lottery system was introduced in 1985 that all NBA teams that missed out on the playoffs remained in the exact spots they were designated, meaning the 10-win/72-loss Philadelphia 76ers received the No. 1 pick, the Los Angeles Lakers kept the No. 2 pick, the Boston Celtics via the Brooklyn Nets got the No. 3 pick, and everyone else stayed in their same spots based on the regular season standings from the [2015–16 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_NBA_season "2015–16 NBA season").

Highlights from the draft include the second Australian No. 1 draft pick ([Ben Simmons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Simmons "Ben Simmons"); the first being [Andrew Bogut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Bogut "Andrew Bogut")), the first Austrian to be selected into the NBA ([Jakob Pöltl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jakob_P%C3%B6ltl "Jakob Pöltl")), the first [Ghanaian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghana "Ghana") to be selected into the NBA ([Ben Bentil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Bentil "Ben Bentil")), the most Frenchmen to be taken overall ([Guerschon Yabusele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guerschon_Yabusele "Guerschon Yabusele"), [Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timoth%C3%A9_Luwawu-Cabarrot "Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot"), [David Michineau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Michineau "David Michineau"), [Isaia Cordinier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isaia_Cordinier "Isaia Cordinier"), [Petr Cornelie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petr_Cornelie "Petr Cornelie")), the first time since the [1990 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_NBA_draft "1990 NBA draft") that an [Egyptian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egypt "Egypt") has been selected into the NBA ([Abdel Nader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdel_Nader "Abdel Nader")), and the first time that two [Chinese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/China "China") players have been selected into the same draft ([Zhou Qi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zhou_Qi "Zhou Qi") and [Wang Zhelin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Zhelin "Wang Zhelin")) since the [2007 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_NBA_draft "2007 NBA draft"). This draft was also notable for providing the most international draft prospects in draft history, with 28 different players representing different countries instead of the United States of America. It beat out the [2004 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_NBA_draft "2004 NBA draft") for the most culturally diverse draft in league history. It was the second time that three players were selected from [Serbian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serbia "Serbia") team [Mega Leks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KK_Mega_Basket "KK Mega Basket") in the same draft ([Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timoth%C3%A9_Luwawu-Cabarrot "Timothé Luwawu-Cabarrot"), [Ivica Zubac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivica_Zubac "Ivica Zubac"), [Rade Zagorac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rade_Zagorac "Rade Zagorac")), the first time being the [2014 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_NBA_draft "2014 NBA draft").

## Eligibility and entrants

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_NBA_draft&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Eligibility and entrants")]

Main article: [Eligibility for the NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eligibility_for_the_NBA_draft "Eligibility for the NBA draft")

The draft is conducted under the eligibility rules established in the league's 2011 [collective bargaining agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Collective_Bargaining_Agreement "NBA Collective Bargaining Agreement") (CBA) with its players union. The CBA that ended the [2011 lockout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_NBA_lockout "2011 NBA lockout") instituted no immediate changes to the draft, but called for a committee of owners and players to discuss future changes.

*   All drafted players must be at least 19 years old during the calendar year of the draft. In terms of dates, players, who are eligible for the 2016 draft, must be born on or before December 31, 1997.
*   On January 13, 2016, the [NCAA Division I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_I "NCAA Division I") council approved a new rule for that division that significantly changed the draft landscape for college players:[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_NBA_draft#cite_note-91)
    *   Declaration for the draft no longer results in automatic loss of college eligibility. As long as a player does not sign a contract with a professional team outside the NBA, or sign with an agent, he will retain college eligibility as long as he makes a timely withdrawal from the draft.
    *   NCAA players now have until 10 days after the end of the [NBA Draft Combine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Draft_Combine "NBA Draft Combine") to withdraw from the draft. For 2016, the withdrawal date was May 25, about five weeks after the previous mid-April deadline.
    *   NCAA players may participate in the draft combine, and will also be allowed to attend one tryout per year with each NBA team without losing college eligibility.
    *   NCAA players may now enter and withdraw from the draft multiple times without loss of eligibility. Previously, the NCAA treated a second declaration of draft eligibility as a permanent loss of college eligibility.

The NBA has since expanded the draft combine to include players with remaining college eligibility (who, like players without college eligibility, can only attend by invitation).[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_NBA_draft#cite_note-92)

### Early entrants

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_NBA_draft&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Early entrants")]

Player who are not automatically eligible must declare their eligibility for the draft by notifying the NBA offices in writing no later than 60 days before the draft. For the 2016 draft, this date fell on April 24. After this date "early entry" players may attend NBA pre-draft camps and individual team workouts to show off their skills and obtain feedback regarding their draft positions. Under the CBA a player may withdraw his name from consideration from the draft at any time before the final declaration date, which is 10 days before the draft. Under newly implemented NCAA rules, players had until May 25 (10 days after the draft combine) to withdraw from the draft and retain college eligibility.

A player who has hired an agent will forfeit his remaining college eligibility regardless of whether he is drafted. The CBA allows a player to withdraw from the draft twice; the 2016 NCAA rule change brought it in line with the CBA on this detail.

#### College underclassmen

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2016_NBA_draft&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: College underclassmen")]

A record-high 162 under-classed draft prospects had declared themselves for eligibility at the April 24 deadline (116 of them being from college), although college players who had not hired agents or signed professional contracts outside the NBA were able to decide to return to college by May 25, 10 days after the end of the [NBA Draft Combine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Draft_Combine "NBA Draft Combine").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_NBA_draft#cite_note-93) At the end of the May 25 deadline, there were 57 players confirming their intentions of returning to school, thus leaving the grand total of underclassmen participating in the NBA draft as 59. Players listed in this region have publicly indicated that they have hired agents, planned to do so around this time, or made themselves their own agents; those who have hired agents and weren't drafted are deemed ineligible to return to NCAA basketball in 2016–17. However, with this year's draft class, it provided the most undrafted college underclassmen out there with 30 people there not being taken at all.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_NBA_draft#cite_note-94)
