## College career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: College career")]

### Liberty

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Liberty")]

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/13/2009_NCAA_Freshman_of_the_Year_Seth_Curry_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-2009_NCAA_Freshman_of_the_Year_Seth_Curry_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2009_NCAA_Freshman_of_the_Year_Seth_Curry_(cropped).jpg)

Curry with [Liberty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_Flames_basketball "Liberty Flames basketball") in 2009 playing at the [Millis Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millis_Center "Millis Center") against [High Point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Point_Panthers_men's_basketball "High Point Panthers men's basketball")

After high school, Curry chose to attend [Liberty University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_University "Liberty University").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-3) In his freshman season at Liberty, he led all freshmen nationally in average points per game scored with 20.2 a game.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-4) Curry broke the Big South Conference single-season scoring record for a freshman. He wore the jersey number 30 at Liberty, the same number his father and older brother wore in their careers.

### Duke

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Duke")]

Curry transferred from Liberty University to [Duke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duke_University "Duke University") after the 2008–09 season.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-5) Per NCAA transfer rules in place at the time, Curry sat out the 2009–10 basketball season. At Duke, he also chose to wear his family number 30.

As a redshirt sophomore, Curry was named a starter after a toe injury sidelined [Kyrie Irving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyrie_Irving "Kyrie Irving"). In a game against [Miami (OH)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_RedHawks_men's_basketball "Miami RedHawks men's basketball"), Curry led the team with 17 points on 57% shooting.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-6) He scored a season high 22 points against [North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_North_Carolina_Tar_Heels_men's_basketball_team "2010–11 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team") on February 9, 2011.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-7) On December 29, 2012, he scored a career-high 31 against [Santa Clara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_Santa_Clara_Broncos_men's_basketball_team "2012–13 Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball team").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-8) At the end of his senior year, Curry was named to the [All-ACC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_All-Atlantic_Coast_Conference_men's_basketball_teams "List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams") first team and was named a second team All-American by _The Sporting News_.

## Professional career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Professional career")]

### Santa Cruz Warriors (2013–2014)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Santa Cruz Warriors (2013–2014)")]

Curry went undrafted in the [2013 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_NBA_draft "2013 NBA draft"). On August 23, 2013, he signed a non-guaranteed contract with the [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_State_Warriors "Golden State Warriors").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-10) He was, however, later waived by Golden State on October 25, 2013, after appearing in six preseason games.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-11)

On November 1, 2013, Curry was acquired by the [Santa Cruz Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Cruz_Warriors "Santa Cruz Warriors") of the [NBA Development League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Development_League "NBA Development League") as an affiliate player.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-12) On November 22, in his D-League debut, Curry recorded 36 points on 12-of-19 shooting, as well as 6 assists and 3 rebounds.

### Memphis Grizzlies (2013–2014)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Memphis Grizzlies (2013–2014)")]

On December 24, 2013, Curry signed with the [Memphis Grizzlies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis_Grizzlies "Memphis Grizzlies").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-13) On January 5, 2014, Curry both made his NBA debut and was waived by the Grizzlies.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-14)

### Return to Santa Cruz (2014)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Return to Santa Cruz (2014)")]

Four days later, Curry was reacquired by the Santa Cruz Warriors. On February 3, 2014, Curry was named to the Futures All-Star roster for the 2014 NBA D-League All-Star Game.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-15)

### Cleveland Cavaliers (2014)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Cleveland Cavaliers (2014)")]

On March 21, 2014, Curry signed a 10-day contract with the [Cleveland Cavaliers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Cavaliers "Cleveland Cavaliers").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-16) On the next day, he appeared in his second NBA game, recording three points in nine minutes of action against the [Houston Rockets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Rockets "Houston Rockets").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-17) The Cavaliers decided not to offer Curry a second 10-day contract,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-18) and he returned to Santa Cruz the following day.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-19) Curry finished the 2013–14 NBA D-League season with averages of 19.7 points, 3.1 rebounds, 5.8 assists and 1.4 steals in 38 games.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-dleague-20)

During his time at Santa Cruz, Curry played in the back court with [Mychel Thompson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mychel_Thompson "Mychel Thompson"). At the same time their respective brothers, Stephen Curry and [Klay Thompson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Klay_Thompson "Klay Thompson"), were playing together in the Golden State backcourt in a tandem nicknamed the "[Splash Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Splash_Brothers "Splash Brothers")."[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-21)

### Erie BayHawks (2014–2015)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Erie BayHawks (2014–2015)")]

In July 2014, Curry joined the [Orlando Magic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic "Orlando Magic") for the [Orlando Summer League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_NBA_Summer_League "2014 NBA Summer League")[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-22) and the [Phoenix Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Suns "Phoenix Suns") for the Las Vegas Summer League.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-23) On September 29, 2014, he signed with the Magic.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-24) On October 7, 2014, Curry's D-League rights were acquired by the Magic's affiliated team, the [Erie BayHawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osceola_Magic "Osceola Magic"), in a trade with the Santa Cruz Warriors.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-25) This was done in preparation for Curry returning to the D-League following training camp, as the Magic were now able to send him to their affiliated team instead of Curry returning to Santa Cruz. As anticipated the Magic waived Curry at the conclusion of training camp on October 25,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-26) and five days later he was acquired by the Erie BayHawks for the start of D-League training camp.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-27) In his debut for Erie in the team's season opener on November 14, Curry scored 23 points on 9-of-24 shooting in a win over the [Idaho Stampede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idaho_Stampede "Idaho Stampede").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-28) On February 4, 2015, he was named to the Futures All-Star team for the 2015 [NBA D-League All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_D-League_All-Star_Game "NBA D-League All-Star Game") for the second time in his career.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-29)

### Phoenix Suns (2015)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Phoenix Suns (2015)")]

On March 11, 2015, Curry signed a 10-day contract with the Phoenix Suns.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-30) He made his Suns debut later that day in a 106–97 win over the [Minnesota Timberwolves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Timberwolves "Minnesota Timberwolves").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-31)

### Return to Erie (2015)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Return to Erie (2015)")]

After Curry's 10-day contract by the Suns expired on March 21, he returned to the BayHawks.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-32) In 43 games for Erie in 2014–15, he averaged 23.8 points, 3.9 rebounds, 4.2 assists and 1.4 steals per game.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-dleague-20)

### Sacramento Kings (2015–2016)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Sacramento Kings (2015–2016)")]

In July 2015, Curry joined the [New Orleans Pelicans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Pelicans "New Orleans Pelicans") for the [2015 NBA Summer League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_Summer_League "2015 NBA Summer League").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-33) After averaging 24.3 points per game in Las Vegas, Curry earned All-NBA Summer League first team honors.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-34) On July 22, he signed a two-year, $2 million guaranteed deal with the [Sacramento Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacramento_Kings "Sacramento Kings").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-36) Considered a "shooting guard trapped in a point guard's body", Curry's three-point shooting was a key reason the Kings signed him, as outside shooting had long been the Kings' Achilles heel.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-37) He made his debut for the Kings on October 30, recording two points, one rebound and one assist in a 132–114 win over the Los Angeles Lakers.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-38) On November 28, he scored 9 points on 3-of-4 shooting and 3-of-3 from three-point range in a loss to the Golden State Warriors.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-39) On February 26, 2016, Curry played extended minutes in the Kings' 117–107 loss to the [Los Angeles Clippers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Clippers "Los Angeles Clippers") due to starting point guard [Rajon Rondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajon_Rondo "Rajon Rondo") sitting out with an injury. In 26 minutes of action off the bench, he recorded a then career-high 19 points and 4 rebounds.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-40) On March 25, he made his first career start, scoring 12 points in 26 minutes against the Phoenix Suns.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-41) Three days later, in just his third NBA start, Curry scored a career-high 21 points in a 105–93 loss to the [Portland Trail Blazers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland_Trail_Blazers "Portland Trail Blazers").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-42) He matched his career high on April 1, scoring 21 points against the [Miami Heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Heat "Miami Heat").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-43) On April 9, he made a career-high six three-pointers and scored 20 points on 6-of-10 shooting off the bench in a 114–112 win over the [Oklahoma City Thunder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma_City_Thunder "Oklahoma City Thunder").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-44) Two days later, he recorded his first career double-double with 20 points and a career-high 15 assists in a career-high 38 minutes of action as the starting point guard, helping the Kings defeat the Phoenix Suns 105–101.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-45)

After the 2015–16 season, Curry declined his $1 million player option for the 2016–17 season in order to become a restricted free agent.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-46) On June 27, 2016, the Kings tendered a qualifying offer to Curry, but on July 3, the team rescinded their qualifying offer, making Curry an unrestricted free agent.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-47)

### Dallas Mavericks (2016–2018)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Dallas Mavericks (2016–2018)")]

On July 15, 2016, Curry signed with the [Dallas Mavericks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Mavericks "Dallas Mavericks").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-48) He made his debut for the Mavericks in their season opener on October 26 against the [Indiana Pacers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana_Pacers "Indiana Pacers"). In 16 minutes off the bench, he recorded seven points, three rebounds, one assist and three steals in a 130–121 overtime loss.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-49) On November 8, he scored a then career-high 23 points in a 109–97 win over the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-50) He tied that mark on November 21, scoring 23 points with five three-pointers as a starter in a 96–91 loss to the [San Antonio Spurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Antonio_Spurs "San Antonio Spurs").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-51) Curry missed four games in early December with a right knee sprain.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-52) On January 29, 2017, he had career highs of 24 points and 10 rebounds to lead the Mavericks to a 105–101 win over San Antonio.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-53) On February 24, 2017, he set a new career high with 31 points in a 97–84 loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-54) Three days later, he had a 29-point effort to go with five three-pointers in a 96–89 win over the Miami Heat.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-55)

On October 7, 2017, Curry was ruled out indefinitely after being diagnosed with a stress reaction of his left [tibia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibia "Tibia").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-56) On February 6, 2018, he was ruled out for the entire season after it was determined he required surgery on his left tibia.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-57)

### Portland Trail Blazers (2018–2019)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Portland Trail Blazers (2018–2019)")]

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Seth_Curry_against_the_Cleveland_Cavaliers_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Seth_Curry_against_the_Cleveland_Cavaliers_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Seth_Curry_against_the_Cleveland_Cavaliers_(cropped).jpg)

Curry with the [Portland Trail Blazers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland_Trail_Blazers "Portland Trail Blazers") in 2019

On July 6, 2018, Curry signed a two-year contract with the [Portland Trail Blazers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland_Trail_Blazers "Portland Trail Blazers"),[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-58) which included a player option for the second year.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-60) On January 26, 2019, he scored 22 points in a 120–111 win over the [Atlanta Hawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Hawks "Atlanta Hawks").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-61) On February 5, he was selected to compete in the [Three-Point Contest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three-Point_Contest "Three-Point Contest") during [All-Star Weekend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_NBA_All-Star_Game "2019 NBA All-Star Game").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-62) On March 9, he scored 22 points in a 127–120 win over the [Phoenix Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Suns "Phoenix Suns").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-63) Curry later went to the [2019 NBA playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_NBA_playoffs "2019 NBA playoffs") with Portland and reached the [Western Conference Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Conference_Finals "NBA Conference Finals") to face his brother Steph and the [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_State_Warriors "Golden State Warriors"), who swept them 4–0 to knock them out of the playoffs.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-McEvoy-64)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-65) This marked the first time a set of brothers faced each other in an NBA playoff series.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-McEvoy-64)

### Return to Dallas (2019–2020)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Return to Dallas (2019–2020)")]

On July 10, 2019, he signed a four-year contract to return to the Dallas Mavericks.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-66) On February 28, 2020, Curry scored a career-high 37 points on 13-of-15 shooting and 8-of-9 from three-point range in a 126–118 loss to the [Miami Heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Heat "Miami Heat").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-67)

### Philadelphia 76ers (2020–2022)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Philadelphia 76ers (2020–2022)")]

On November 18, 2020, Curry was traded to the [Philadelphia 76ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers") in exchange for [Josh Richardson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Richardson "Josh Richardson") and the draft rights to [Tyler Bey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyler_Bey "Tyler Bey").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-68) It signified playing under his father-in-law [Doc Rivers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doc_Rivers "Doc Rivers"), who was hired as head coach that October.

In a Game 5 elimination of the [Washington Wizards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Wizards "Washington Wizards") in the first round of the 2020-21 playoffs, he registered 30 points while shooting 10-17 overall and 3-6 from three.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-69) On June 16, 2021, during the second round, Curry recorded a new playoff career high of 36 points in a Game 5 losing effort against the Atlanta Hawks.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-70) He increased his scoring average in the seven-game series to 21.0 ppg, while maintaining an efficient 61% from the field and 59.6% from three on 7.4 attempts per game.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-71)

His 2021-22 time as a 76er marked his most minutes played per game (34.8) and points per game (15.0) before or since, as he continued to start in all 102 games he appeared in dating back to the previous season. Curry left the team as the all-time leader in 3-point percentage in franchise history at 42.6%, tying him with [Dana Barros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dana_Barros "Dana Barros").[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-72)

### Brooklyn Nets (2022–2023)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Brooklyn Nets (2022–2023)")]

On February 10, 2022, Curry was traded, along with [Ben Simmons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Simmons "Ben Simmons"), [Andre Drummond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andre_Drummond "Andre Drummond") and two future first-round picks, to the [Brooklyn Nets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_Nets "Brooklyn Nets") in exchange for [James Harden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Harden "James Harden") and [Paul Millsap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Millsap "Paul Millsap").[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-73) In his debut for the Nets on February 14, Curry led the team in scoring with 23 points in a 109–85 win against the [Sacramento Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacramento_Kings "Sacramento Kings") and helped the team end an 11-game losing streak.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-74) On May 9, he underwent left ankle surgery.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-75)

### Third stint with Dallas (2023–2024)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Third stint with Dallas (2023–2024)")]

On July 14, 2023, he signed with the Dallas Mavericks for a third time.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-76)

### Charlotte Hornets (2024–2025)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Charlotte Hornets (2024–2025)")]

On February 8, 2024, Curry was traded to his hometown team [Charlotte Hornets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte_Hornets "Charlotte Hornets") alongside [Grant Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grant_Williams_(basketball) "Grant Williams (basketball)") and a 2027 first-round pick in exchange for [P. J. Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P._J._Washington "P. J. Washington") and two future second-round picks.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-77) On June 28, 2024, he was waived by the Hornets.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-78) However, he was re-signed on July 15, 2024.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-79) On October 24, 2024, Curry scored a season-high 15 points against the Miami Heat.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-80) Curry led the NBA in 3-point field goal percentage for the [2024-25 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_NBA_season "2024–25 NBA season"), converting 45.6% of his 3-point attempts.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-81)

### Golden State Warriors (2025–2026)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Golden State Warriors (2025–2026)")]

On October 1, 2025, Curry signed a one-year contract with the [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_State_Warriors "Golden State Warriors"), joining his brother [Stephen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Curry "Stephen Curry") in their NBA careers for the first time since 2013.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-82)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-83) The Warriors waived him on October 18 with the expectation that they would re-sign him within the first few months of the season. Due to [salary cap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_salary_cap "NBA salary cap") restrictions, they could not afford another veteran minimum contract until early November.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-84) Curry re-signed with the Warriors on a rest of season deal on December 1.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-85) On December 2, Curry made his Warriors debut, putting up 14 points on 6-of-7 shooting, including 2-of-3 from three, along with 2 rebounds, 2 assists, and one steal in 17 minutes off the bench in a loss to the [Oklahoma City Thunder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_Oklahoma_City_Thunder_season "2025–26 Oklahoma City Thunder season").[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-86)

## National team career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: National team career")]

Curry competed for the United States in the 2009 [FIBA Under-19 World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIBA_Under-19_World_Championship "FIBA Under-19 World Championship") in [New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand "New Zealand"), winning the tournament by defeating Greece 88–80 in the final.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-87) For the tournament, Curry averaged 9.0 points, 2.2 rebounds and 1.1 assists per game.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-88)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Personal life")]

On September 14, 2019, Curry married former professional volleyball player Callie Rivers, daughter of his former head coach [Doc Rivers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doc_Rivers "Doc Rivers") and sister of his former Duke teammate [Austin Rivers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_Rivers "Austin Rivers").[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-89)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-90) They have three children.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-91)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-92)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-93) Curry's older brother, [Stephen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Curry "Stephen Curry"), is his former teammate and the starting [point guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Point_guard "Point guard") for the [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_State_Warriors "Golden State Warriors"), while his younger sister, Sydel, played college volleyball at [Elon University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elon_University "Elon University")[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-94)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-95) and is married to professional basketball player [Damion Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damion_Lee "Damion Lee"). Curry is a [Pentecostal Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentecostal_Christian "Pentecostal Christian").[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-96)

**Seth Adham Curry** (born August 23, 1990) is an American professional [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") player who last played for the [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_State_Warriors "Golden State Warriors") of the [National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") (NBA). He played [college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") for one year at [Liberty University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_Flames_basketball "Liberty Flames basketball") before transferring to [Duke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duke_Blue_Devils_men's_basketball "Duke Blue Devils men's basketball"). He is the son of former NBA player [Dell Curry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dell_Curry "Dell Curry") and the younger brother of NBA player [Stephen Curry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Curry "Stephen Curry"). He currently ranks seventh in NBA history in career three-point field goal percentage.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-1)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Curry is the son of former National Basketball Association (NBA) player [Dell Curry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dell_Curry "Dell Curry") and former [Virginia Tech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Tech "Virginia Tech") women's volleyball player [Sonya Curry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonya_Curry "Sonya Curry").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-2) He grew up in [Charlotte, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte,_North_Carolina "Charlotte, North Carolina"), while his father, Dell, played for the [Charlotte Hornets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte_Hornets "Charlotte Hornets"). As a child, Curry's father would take him and his older brother, [Stephen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Curry "Stephen Curry"), to his games where they would often shoot around with the team in warm-ups. Curry is a 2008 graduate of [Charlotte Christian School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte_Christian_School "Charlotte Christian School") where he was a three-year starter for the Knights' basketball team. His senior year, Curry averaged 22.3 points, 5.0 rebounds, and 5.0 assists while shooting 52 percent from the field. At the end of the season, he earned all-conference, all-state, and first team SAA All-American accolades. In his three years on varsity, Charlotte Christian amassed a 105–24 overall record including a state final appearance in 2006. Curry was also on the Charlotte Christian academic honor roll all four years.

## College career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: College career")]

### Liberty

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Liberty")]

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/13/2009_NCAA_Freshman_of_the_Year_Seth_Curry_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-2009_NCAA_Freshman_of_the_Year_Seth_Curry_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2009_NCAA_Freshman_of_the_Year_Seth_Curry_(cropped).jpg)

Curry with [Liberty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_Flames_basketball "Liberty Flames basketball") in 2009 playing at the [Millis Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millis_Center "Millis Center") against [High Point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Point_Panthers_men's_basketball "High Point Panthers men's basketball")

After high school, Curry chose to attend [Liberty University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_University "Liberty University").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-3) In his freshman season at Liberty, he led all freshmen nationally in average points per game scored with 20.2 a game.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-4) Curry broke the Big South Conference single-season scoring record for a freshman. He wore the jersey number 30 at Liberty, the same number his father and older brother wore in their careers.

### Duke

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Duke")]

Curry transferred from Liberty University to [Duke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duke_University "Duke University") after the 2008–09 season.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-5) Per NCAA transfer rules in place at the time, Curry sat out the 2009–10 basketball season. At Duke, he also chose to wear his family number 30.

As a redshirt sophomore, Curry was named a starter after a toe injury sidelined [Kyrie Irving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyrie_Irving "Kyrie Irving"). In a game against [Miami (OH)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_RedHawks_men's_basketball "Miami RedHawks men's basketball"), Curry led the team with 17 points on 57% shooting.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-6) He scored a season high 22 points against [North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_North_Carolina_Tar_Heels_men's_basketball_team "2010–11 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team") on February 9, 2011.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-7) On December 29, 2012, he scored a career-high 31 against [Santa Clara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_Santa_Clara_Broncos_men's_basketball_team "2012–13 Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball team").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-8) At the end of his senior year, Curry was named to the [All-ACC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_All-Atlantic_Coast_Conference_men's_basketball_teams "List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams") first team and was named a second team All-American by _The Sporting News_.

## Professional career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Professional career")]

### Santa Cruz Warriors (2013–2014)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Santa Cruz Warriors (2013–2014)")]

Curry went undrafted in the [2013 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_NBA_draft "2013 NBA draft"). On August 23, 2013, he signed a non-guaranteed contract with the [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_State_Warriors "Golden State Warriors").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-10) He was, however, later waived by Golden State on October 25, 2013, after appearing in six preseason games.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-11)

On November 1, 2013, Curry was acquired by the [Santa Cruz Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Cruz_Warriors "Santa Cruz Warriors") of the [NBA Development League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Development_League "NBA Development League") as an affiliate player.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-12) On November 22, in his D-League debut, Curry recorded 36 points on 12-of-19 shooting, as well as 6 assists and 3 rebounds.

### Memphis Grizzlies (2013–2014)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Memphis Grizzlies (2013–2014)")]

On December 24, 2013, Curry signed with the [Memphis Grizzlies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis_Grizzlies "Memphis Grizzlies").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-13) On January 5, 2014, Curry both made his NBA debut and was waived by the Grizzlies.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-14)

### Return to Santa Cruz (2014)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Return to Santa Cruz (2014)")]

Four days later, Curry was reacquired by the Santa Cruz Warriors. On February 3, 2014, Curry was named to the Futures All-Star roster for the 2014 NBA D-League All-Star Game.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-15)

### Cleveland Cavaliers (2014)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Cleveland Cavaliers (2014)")]

On March 21, 2014, Curry signed a 10-day contract with the [Cleveland Cavaliers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Cavaliers "Cleveland Cavaliers").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-16) On the next day, he appeared in his second NBA game, recording three points in nine minutes of action against the [Houston Rockets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Rockets "Houston Rockets").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-17) The Cavaliers decided not to offer Curry a second 10-day contract,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-18) and he returned to Santa Cruz the following day.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-19) Curry finished the 2013–14 NBA D-League season with averages of 19.7 points, 3.1 rebounds, 5.8 assists and 1.4 steals in 38 games.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-dleague-20)

During his time at Santa Cruz, Curry played in the back court with [Mychel Thompson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mychel_Thompson "Mychel Thompson"). At the same time their respective brothers, Stephen Curry and [Klay Thompson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Klay_Thompson "Klay Thompson"), were playing together in the Golden State backcourt in a tandem nicknamed the "[Splash Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Splash_Brothers "Splash Brothers")."[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-21)

### Erie BayHawks (2014–2015)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Erie BayHawks (2014–2015)")]

In July 2014, Curry joined the [Orlando Magic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orlando_Magic "Orlando Magic") for the [Orlando Summer League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_NBA_Summer_League "2014 NBA Summer League")[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-22) and the [Phoenix Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Suns "Phoenix Suns") for the Las Vegas Summer League.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-23) On September 29, 2014, he signed with the Magic.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-24) On October 7, 2014, Curry's D-League rights were acquired by the Magic's affiliated team, the [Erie BayHawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osceola_Magic "Osceola Magic"), in a trade with the Santa Cruz Warriors.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-25) This was done in preparation for Curry returning to the D-League following training camp, as the Magic were now able to send him to their affiliated team instead of Curry returning to Santa Cruz. As anticipated the Magic waived Curry at the conclusion of training camp on October 25,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-26) and five days later he was acquired by the Erie BayHawks for the start of D-League training camp.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-27) In his debut for Erie in the team's season opener on November 14, Curry scored 23 points on 9-of-24 shooting in a win over the [Idaho Stampede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idaho_Stampede "Idaho Stampede").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-28) On February 4, 2015, he was named to the Futures All-Star team for the 2015 [NBA D-League All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_D-League_All-Star_Game "NBA D-League All-Star Game") for the second time in his career.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-29)

### Phoenix Suns (2015)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Phoenix Suns (2015)")]

On March 11, 2015, Curry signed a 10-day contract with the Phoenix Suns.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-30) He made his Suns debut later that day in a 106–97 win over the [Minnesota Timberwolves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Timberwolves "Minnesota Timberwolves").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-31)

### Return to Erie (2015)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Return to Erie (2015)")]

After Curry's 10-day contract by the Suns expired on March 21, he returned to the BayHawks.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-32) In 43 games for Erie in 2014–15, he averaged 23.8 points, 3.9 rebounds, 4.2 assists and 1.4 steals per game.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-dleague-20)

### Sacramento Kings (2015–2016)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Sacramento Kings (2015–2016)")]

In July 2015, Curry joined the [New Orleans Pelicans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Pelicans "New Orleans Pelicans") for the [2015 NBA Summer League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_NBA_Summer_League "2015 NBA Summer League").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-33) After averaging 24.3 points per game in Las Vegas, Curry earned All-NBA Summer League first team honors.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-34) On July 22, he signed a two-year, $2 million guaranteed deal with the [Sacramento Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacramento_Kings "Sacramento Kings").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-36) Considered a "shooting guard trapped in a point guard's body", Curry's three-point shooting was a key reason the Kings signed him, as outside shooting had long been the Kings' Achilles heel.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-37) He made his debut for the Kings on October 30, recording two points, one rebound and one assist in a 132–114 win over the Los Angeles Lakers.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-38) On November 28, he scored 9 points on 3-of-4 shooting and 3-of-3 from three-point range in a loss to the Golden State Warriors.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-39) On February 26, 2016, Curry played extended minutes in the Kings' 117–107 loss to the [Los Angeles Clippers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Clippers "Los Angeles Clippers") due to starting point guard [Rajon Rondo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajon_Rondo "Rajon Rondo") sitting out with an injury. In 26 minutes of action off the bench, he recorded a then career-high 19 points and 4 rebounds.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-40) On March 25, he made his first career start, scoring 12 points in 26 minutes against the Phoenix Suns.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-41) Three days later, in just his third NBA start, Curry scored a career-high 21 points in a 105–93 loss to the [Portland Trail Blazers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland_Trail_Blazers "Portland Trail Blazers").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-42) He matched his career high on April 1, scoring 21 points against the [Miami Heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Heat "Miami Heat").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-43) On April 9, he made a career-high six three-pointers and scored 20 points on 6-of-10 shooting off the bench in a 114–112 win over the [Oklahoma City Thunder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma_City_Thunder "Oklahoma City Thunder").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-44) Two days later, he recorded his first career double-double with 20 points and a career-high 15 assists in a career-high 38 minutes of action as the starting point guard, helping the Kings defeat the Phoenix Suns 105–101.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-45)

After the 2015–16 season, Curry declined his $1 million player option for the 2016–17 season in order to become a restricted free agent.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-46) On June 27, 2016, the Kings tendered a qualifying offer to Curry, but on July 3, the team rescinded their qualifying offer, making Curry an unrestricted free agent.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-47)

### Dallas Mavericks (2016–2018)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Dallas Mavericks (2016–2018)")]

On July 15, 2016, Curry signed with the [Dallas Mavericks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Mavericks "Dallas Mavericks").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-48) He made his debut for the Mavericks in their season opener on October 26 against the [Indiana Pacers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana_Pacers "Indiana Pacers"). In 16 minutes off the bench, he recorded seven points, three rebounds, one assist and three steals in a 130–121 overtime loss.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-49) On November 8, he scored a then career-high 23 points in a 109–97 win over the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-50) He tied that mark on November 21, scoring 23 points with five three-pointers as a starter in a 96–91 loss to the [San Antonio Spurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Antonio_Spurs "San Antonio Spurs").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-51) Curry missed four games in early December with a right knee sprain.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-52) On January 29, 2017, he had career highs of 24 points and 10 rebounds to lead the Mavericks to a 105–101 win over San Antonio.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-53) On February 24, 2017, he set a new career high with 31 points in a 97–84 loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-54) Three days later, he had a 29-point effort to go with five three-pointers in a 96–89 win over the Miami Heat.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-55)

On October 7, 2017, Curry was ruled out indefinitely after being diagnosed with a stress reaction of his left [tibia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibia "Tibia").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-56) On February 6, 2018, he was ruled out for the entire season after it was determined he required surgery on his left tibia.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-57)

### Portland Trail Blazers (2018–2019)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Portland Trail Blazers (2018–2019)")]

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/01/Seth_Curry_against_the_Cleveland_Cavaliers_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Seth_Curry_against_the_Cleveland_Cavaliers_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Seth_Curry_against_the_Cleveland_Cavaliers_(cropped).jpg)

Curry with the [Portland Trail Blazers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland_Trail_Blazers "Portland Trail Blazers") in 2019

On July 6, 2018, Curry signed a two-year contract with the [Portland Trail Blazers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland_Trail_Blazers "Portland Trail Blazers"),[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-58) which included a player option for the second year.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-60) On January 26, 2019, he scored 22 points in a 120–111 win over the [Atlanta Hawks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta_Hawks "Atlanta Hawks").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-61) On February 5, he was selected to compete in the [Three-Point Contest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Three-Point_Contest "Three-Point Contest") during [All-Star Weekend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_NBA_All-Star_Game "2019 NBA All-Star Game").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-62) On March 9, he scored 22 points in a 127–120 win over the [Phoenix Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Suns "Phoenix Suns").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-63) Curry later went to the [2019 NBA playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_NBA_playoffs "2019 NBA playoffs") with Portland and reached the [Western Conference Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Conference_Finals "NBA Conference Finals") to face his brother Steph and the [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_State_Warriors "Golden State Warriors"), who swept them 4–0 to knock them out of the playoffs.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-McEvoy-64)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-65) This marked the first time a set of brothers faced each other in an NBA playoff series.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-McEvoy-64)

### Return to Dallas (2019–2020)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Return to Dallas (2019–2020)")]

On July 10, 2019, he signed a four-year contract to return to the Dallas Mavericks.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-66) On February 28, 2020, Curry scored a career-high 37 points on 13-of-15 shooting and 8-of-9 from three-point range in a 126–118 loss to the [Miami Heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miami_Heat "Miami Heat").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-67)

### Philadelphia 76ers (2020–2022)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Philadelphia 76ers (2020–2022)")]

On November 18, 2020, Curry was traded to the [Philadelphia 76ers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers") in exchange for [Josh Richardson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Josh_Richardson "Josh Richardson") and the draft rights to [Tyler Bey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyler_Bey "Tyler Bey").[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-68) It signified playing under his father-in-law [Doc Rivers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doc_Rivers "Doc Rivers"), who was hired as head coach that October.

In a Game 5 elimination of the [Washington Wizards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Wizards "Washington Wizards") in the first round of the 2020-21 playoffs, he registered 30 points while shooting 10-17 overall and 3-6 from three.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-69) On June 16, 2021, during the second round, Curry recorded a new playoff career high of 36 points in a Game 5 losing effort against the Atlanta Hawks.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-70) He increased his scoring average in the seven-game series to 21.0 ppg, while maintaining an efficient 61% from the field and 59.6% from three on 7.4 attempts per game.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-71)

His 2021-22 time as a 76er marked his most minutes played per game (34.8) and points per game (15.0) before or since, as he continued to start in all 102 games he appeared in dating back to the previous season. Curry left the team as the all-time leader in 3-point percentage in franchise history at 42.6%, tying him with [Dana Barros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dana_Barros "Dana Barros").[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-72)

### Brooklyn Nets (2022–2023)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Brooklyn Nets (2022–2023)")]

On February 10, 2022, Curry was traded, along with [Ben Simmons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Simmons "Ben Simmons"), [Andre Drummond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andre_Drummond "Andre Drummond") and two future first-round picks, to the [Brooklyn Nets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_Nets "Brooklyn Nets") in exchange for [James Harden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Harden "James Harden") and [Paul Millsap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Millsap "Paul Millsap").[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-73) In his debut for the Nets on February 14, Curry led the team in scoring with 23 points in a 109–85 win against the [Sacramento Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacramento_Kings "Sacramento Kings") and helped the team end an 11-game losing streak.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-74) On May 9, he underwent left ankle surgery.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-75)

### Third stint with Dallas (2023–2024)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Third stint with Dallas (2023–2024)")]

On July 14, 2023, he signed with the Dallas Mavericks for a third time.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-76)

### Charlotte Hornets (2024–2025)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Charlotte Hornets (2024–2025)")]

On February 8, 2024, Curry was traded to his hometown team [Charlotte Hornets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte_Hornets "Charlotte Hornets") alongside [Grant Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grant_Williams_(basketball) "Grant Williams (basketball)") and a 2027 first-round pick in exchange for [P. J. Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P._J._Washington "P. J. Washington") and two future second-round picks.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-77) On June 28, 2024, he was waived by the Hornets.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-78) However, he was re-signed on July 15, 2024.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-79) On October 24, 2024, Curry scored a season-high 15 points against the Miami Heat.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-80) Curry led the NBA in 3-point field goal percentage for the [2024-25 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_NBA_season "2024–25 NBA season"), converting 45.6% of his 3-point attempts.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-81)

### Golden State Warriors (2025–2026)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Golden State Warriors (2025–2026)")]

On October 1, 2025, Curry signed a one-year contract with the [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_State_Warriors "Golden State Warriors"), joining his brother [Stephen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Curry "Stephen Curry") in their NBA careers for the first time since 2013.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-82)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-83) The Warriors waived him on October 18 with the expectation that they would re-sign him within the first few months of the season. Due to [salary cap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_salary_cap "NBA salary cap") restrictions, they could not afford another veteran minimum contract until early November.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-84) Curry re-signed with the Warriors on a rest of season deal on December 1.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-85) On December 2, Curry made his Warriors debut, putting up 14 points on 6-of-7 shooting, including 2-of-3 from three, along with 2 rebounds, 2 assists, and one steal in 17 minutes off the bench in a loss to the [Oklahoma City Thunder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_Oklahoma_City_Thunder_season "2025–26 Oklahoma City Thunder season").[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-86)

## National team career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: National team career")]

Curry competed for the United States in the 2009 [FIBA Under-19 World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIBA_Under-19_World_Championship "FIBA Under-19 World Championship") in [New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand "New Zealand"), winning the tournament by defeating Greece 88–80 in the final.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-87) For the tournament, Curry averaged 9.0 points, 2.2 rebounds and 1.1 assists per game.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-88)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Seth_Curry&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Personal life")]

On September 14, 2019, Curry married former professional volleyball player Callie Rivers, daughter of his former head coach [Doc Rivers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doc_Rivers "Doc Rivers") and sister of his former Duke teammate [Austin Rivers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austin_Rivers "Austin Rivers").[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-89)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-90) They have three children.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-91)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-92)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-93) Curry's older brother, [Stephen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Curry "Stephen Curry"), is his former teammate and the starting [point guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Point_guard "Point guard") for the [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_State_Warriors "Golden State Warriors"), while his younger sister, Sydel, played college volleyball at [Elon University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elon_University "Elon University")[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-94)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-95) and is married to professional basketball player [Damion Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damion_Lee "Damion Lee"). Curry is a [Pentecostal Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentecostal_Christian "Pentecostal Christian").[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seth_Curry#cite_note-96)
