**Dragan Bender** (born 17 November 1997) is a Croatian former professional [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") player. He stands 7 ft 0 in (2.13 m) and played the [power forward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_forward_(basketball) "Power forward (basketball)") and [center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Center_(basketball) "Center (basketball)") positions. He was selected by the [Phoenix Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Suns "Phoenix Suns") with the fourth overall pick in the 2016 NBA draft but only played four years in the league. Bender represents the [Croatian national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_men's_national_basketball_team "Croatia men's national basketball team"), with experience in the [FIBA Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIBA_Europe "FIBA Europe") junior tournaments. Before playing in Israel, he competed with multiple teams in Croatia and in [Nikola Vujčić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikola_Vuj%C4%8Di%C4%87 "Nikola Vujčić")'s academy.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Bender was born on 17 November 1997, in [Čapljina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C4%8Capljina "Čapljina"), [Bosnia and Herzegovina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Bosnia and Herzegovina"), and he later moved to [Split, Croatia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Split,_Croatia "Split, Croatia").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-NBA_Draft-1) At 12 years of age, he started playing at [Nikola Vujčić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikola_Vuj%C4%8Di%C4%87 "Nikola Vujčić")'s basketball academy as a [point guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Point_guard "Point guard").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-jpost-2) Vujčić was a former [Maccabi Tel Aviv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maccabi_Tel_Aviv_B.C. "Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.") star and became Bender's guardian.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-br-3) At the academy, Bender became a more versatile player and he "learned how to play all the positions on the court."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-fastbreak-4) Bender played there along with his older brother, Ivan, with Bender also playing against guys that were Ivan's age when he first started playing.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-si-5) Bender also played with the [KK Split](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KK_Split "KK Split") youth teams at this time, and he appeared for the Croatian under-16 national basketball team.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-yahoo-6) He idolized and modeled his game after [Toni Kukoč](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toni_Kuko%C4%8D "Toni Kukoč"), a former Croatian [NBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA "NBA") player, while growing up and watched his old game tape.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-jpost-2) He mostly watched [EuroLeague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EuroLeague "EuroLeague") games but would sometimes tune into the NBA as well. One of his favorite EuroLeague players was [Šarūnas Jasikevičius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%A0ar%C5%ABnas_Jasikevi%C4%8Dius "Šarūnas Jasikevičius").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-si-5)

## Professional career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Professional career")]

### Split (2012–2013)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Split (2012–2013)")]

Bender made his professional debut at 15 years of age with [KK Split](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KK_Split "KK Split"). He played only a total of six minutes and added two points and one rebound.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-yahoo-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-eurobasket-7)

### Kaštela (2013–2014)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Kaštela (2013–2014)")]

For the following season, Bender remained in Croatia and signed with [KK Kaštela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KK_Ka%C5%A1tela "KK Kaštela"), who played in the country's second-best league.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-euroleague-8) With his help, the team was promoted to the [A-1 Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-1_Liga "A-1 Liga"), the top league in Croatia.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-kastela-9) Most notably, he made a game-winning shot with three seconds remaining against [KK Gorica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KK_Gorica "KK Gorica") to help his team secure the promotion.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-kastela-9) Later, in February 2014, Bender joined the [KK Cedevita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KK_Cedevita "KK Cedevita") junior team for the [Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euroleague_Basketball_Next_Generation_Tournament "Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament"). He put up 21 points, 9 rebounds, and 6 assists vs the junior team of the Serbian club [KK Mega Basket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KK_Mega_Basket "KK Mega Basket").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-10)

### Ironi Ramat Gan (2014–2016)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Ironi Ramat Gan (2014–2016)")]

In 2014, Bender signed a seven-year contract with [Maccabi Tel Aviv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maccabi_Tel_Aviv_B.C. "Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C."), a team that played in the [Israeli Basketball Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Basketball_Premier_League "Israeli Basketball Premier League") and the [EuroLeague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EuroLeague "EuroLeague").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-future-11) He was soon [loaned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loan_(sports) "Loan (sports)") to [Ironi Ramat Gan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ironi_Ramat_Gan "Ironi Ramat Gan") of the [Liga Leumit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liga_Leumit_(basketball) "Liga Leumit (basketball)"), the second-tier-level league in Israel, for the 2014–15 season.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-12) He made his debut on 21 October 2014, posting 13 points, 13 rebounds, and 4 assists vs [Ramat HaSharon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.S._Ramat_HaSharon "A.S. Ramat HaSharon").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-13) He recorded another [double-double](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double-double_(basketball) "Double-double (basketball)") on 12 December, with 23 points and 12 rebounds in a win over [Maccabi Ra'anana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maccabi_Ra'anana "Maccabi Ra'anana").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-14) Bender scored a season-high 25 points as his team defeated [Barak Netanya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elitzur_Netanya_B.C. "Elitzur Netanya B.C.") by one point on 1 January 2015.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-15) After 28 games, he finished the season averaging 9.7 points, 7.4 rebounds, 2.6 assists, and 1.1 blocks.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-eurobasket-7) As the season came to a close, Bender returned to Maccabi Tel Aviv.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-16)

### Maccabi Tel Aviv (2015–2016)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Maccabi Tel Aviv (2015–2016)")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/88/Bender_BoxOut.JPG/250px-Bender_BoxOut.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bender_BoxOut.JPG)

Bender (#3) with Maccabi Tel Aviv in 2015

Bender debuted for Maccabi Tel Aviv in the Israeli Premier League on 11 October 2015, with 5 points, 3 rebounds, and 3 blocks in a win over [Maccabi Kiryat Gat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maccabi_Kiryat_Gat_B.C. "Maccabi Kiryat Gat B.C.").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-17) He scored double figures for the first time with the team in a rematch with Kiryat Gat, adding 15 points.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-yahoo-6)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-18) Bender scored a season-high 16 points on 31 December 2015, as his team defeated [Hapoel Holon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hapoel_Holon "Hapoel Holon").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-19) In 2015–16, he helped Maccabi Tel Aviv repeat as winners in the [2016 Israeli State Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Israeli_Basketball_State_Cup "2015–16 Israeli Basketball State Cup"), and he was named a foreign All-Star for the 2016 Israeli All-Star game.

On 6 April 2016, Bender declared for the 2016 NBA draft.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-20) His contract with Maccabi Tel Aviv was later bought out for $1.3 million.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-21)

### Phoenix Suns (2016–2019)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Phoenix Suns (2016–2019)")]

On 23 June 2016, Bender was selected by the [Phoenix Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Suns "Phoenix Suns") with the fourth overall pick in the 2016 NBA draft.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-22) He was widely billed as the best international prospect available in the draft, highly valued for his ability to shoot the ball in various ways as a big man, as well as his overall untapped potential in other facets of the game.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-23) As the fourth overall pick, Bender became the Suns' highest-selected rookie since [Armen Gilliam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armen_Gilliam "Armen Gilliam") was taken second overall in [1987](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_NBA_draft "1987 NBA draft"),[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-24) and the highest-selected Croatian to be taken in an NBA draft. On 7 July, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Suns and joined the team for the [2016 NBA Summer League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_NBA_Summer_League "2016 NBA Summer League").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-25) Bender made his debut for the Suns in their season opener on 26 October 2016, scoring 10 points on 4-of-5 shooting in a 113–94 loss to the [Sacramento Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacramento_Kings "Sacramento Kings").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-26) With Bender playing alongside [Devin Booker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Booker "Devin Booker") and fellow rookie [Marquese Chriss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marquese_Chriss "Marquese Chriss"), the Suns became the first NBA team to get three teenagers on the floor in the same game.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-27) Bender also joined Booker and [Giannis Antetokounmpo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giannis_Antetokounmpo "Giannis Antetokounmpo") as the only 18-year-olds to score 10 points in a game since 2006–07.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-28) He had his second 10-point game of the season on 8 November in a 124–121 loss to the [Portland Trail Blazers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland_Trail_Blazers "Portland Trail Blazers").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-29) He then had his third 10-point game of the season on 3 December in a 138–109 loss to the [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_State_Warriors "Golden State Warriors").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-30) On 26 December, Bender recorded his first career double-double with season highs of 11 points and 13 rebounds in a 131–115 loss to the [Houston Rockets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Rockets "Houston Rockets").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-31) On 8 February 2017, Bender underwent a successful routine arthroscopic procedure on his right ankle to remove a bone spur. He was subsequently ruled out for approximately four to six weeks.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-32) He returned to action on 2 April 2017, against Houston.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-33)

In July 2017, Bender re-joined the Suns for the [2017 NBA Summer League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_NBA_Summer_League "2017 NBA Summer League").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-34) In five games, he averaged 14.2 points, 6.0 rebounds, and 2.4 assists per game. On 13 November 2017, Bender scored a career-high 15 points in a 100–93 loss to the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-35) On 16 December 2017, he set a new career high with 17 points in a 108–106 win over the [Minnesota Timberwolves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Timberwolves "Minnesota Timberwolves").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-36) On 7 January 2018, he scored 17 of his then career-high 20 points in the second half of the Suns' 114–100 win over the [Oklahoma City Thunder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma_City_Thunder "Oklahoma City Thunder"). He made a career-best six 3-pointers, going 5 of 6 in the second half.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-37) On 10 February 2018, he scored a career-high 23 points in a 123–113 loss to the [Denver Nuggets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Nuggets "Denver Nuggets").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-38) On 8 April 2018, Bender recorded 14 points and a career-high 14 rebounds in a 117–100 loss to the [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_State_Warriors "Golden State Warriors").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-39)

In July 2018, Bender re-joined the Suns for the [2018 NBA Summer League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_NBA_Summer_League "2018 NBA Summer League").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-40) On 30 October 2018, the Suns declined Bender's $5.9 million fourth year rookie option, making him a free agent after the season. On 5 April 2019, Bender recorded a career-high seven blocks in a 133–126 overtime win over the [New Orleans Pelicans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Pelicans "New Orleans Pelicans").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-41)

### Milwaukee Bucks (2019–2020)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Milwaukee Bucks (2019–2020)")]

In July 2019, Bender signed a two-year minimum deal with the [Milwaukee Bucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Bucks "Milwaukee Bucks").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-42) The first year of Bender's deal was partially guaranteed, but it became fully guaranteed when the Bucks did not waive Bender by 7 January, while the second is non-guaranteed.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-43) Bender was assigned to the [Wisconsin Herd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wisconsin_Herd "Wisconsin Herd") for the start of the [NBA G League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_G_League "NBA G League") season. On 10 February 2020, the [Milwaukee Bucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Bucks "Milwaukee Bucks") announced that they had waived Bender.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-44)

### Golden State Warriors (2020)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Golden State Warriors (2020)")]

On 23 February 2020, the [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_State_Warriors "Golden State Warriors") announced that they had signed Bender to a 10-day contract.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-45) In his first game he played against his former team, the [Phoenix Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Suns "Phoenix Suns"), he recorded 13 points and 9 rebounds in a 115–99 win on 29 February.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-46) He then acquired a second 10-day contract on 5 March 2020. In his last game before the [NBA season was suspended](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suspension_of_the_2019%E2%80%9320_NBA_season "Suspension of the 2019–20 NBA season") due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_the_United_States "COVID-19 pandemic in the United States"), Bender tied his career high with 23 points on 8-of-12 shooting and added 7 rebounds in a 131–107 loss to the [Los Angeles Clippers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Clippers "Los Angeles Clippers") on 10 March.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-47) The season was suspended while Bender was still on contract, and he became a free agent before the season restarted in July.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-48) Bender's short and uneventful NBA career marked him as a high-profile draft bust.

### Maccabi Tel Aviv (2020–2021)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Maccabi Tel Aviv (2020–2021)")]

On 23 September 2020, Bender returned to the Israeli team [Maccabi Tel Aviv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maccabi_Tel_Aviv "Maccabi Tel Aviv").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-49) During the 2020–21 season, he averaged 6.6 points, 3.8 rebounds over 34 EuroLeague games. He suffered a season-ending injury in May 2021 that caused him to miss the entire 2021–22 season.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-50)

### Obradoiro (2022)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Obradoiro (2022)")]

On August 23, 2022, Bender signed with [Monbus Obradoiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obradoiro_CAB "Obradoiro CAB") of the Spanish [Liga ACB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liga_ACB "Liga ACB").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-51) On December 11, he suffered a [torn ACL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anterior_cruciate_ligament_injury "Anterior cruciate ligament injury") injury in his left knee and thus finished a season averaging 17.2 points and 6.6 rebounds on 52.7% shooting from the field in 10 games played for Obradoiro.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-aclinjury-2024update-52)

## National team career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: National team career")]

### Junior national team

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Junior national team")]

Bender competed for the Croatian national Under-16 team at the [2012 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_FIBA_Europe_Under-16_Championship "2012 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship"). in Latvia and Lithuania. Through five contests, he averaged 2.8 points and 1.4 rebounds in 5.6 minutes per game.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-53) The following year, he came back to the [2013 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FIBA_Europe_Under-16_Championship "2013 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship") in Ukraine, improving through 9 games to 9.8 points, 10.8 rebounds and 4.1 assists in 35.4 minutes per game.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-54) Bender improved even further, while playing with the Croatian national Under-18 team, at the [2014 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIBA_Europe_Under-18_Championship "2014 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship") in Turkey. In 9 games, he averaged 14.4 points, 10.4 rebounds and 4.9 assists in 29 minutes per game, helping his team win the bronze medal, and being named to All-Tournament Team in the process.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-55)

In 2015, Bender was selected by Croatia for the [2015 FIBA Under-19 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_FIBA_Under-19_World_Championship "2015 FIBA Under-19 World Championship") in [Crete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crete "Crete"), Greece, but he was forced to withdraw because the team's players were obliged to wear [Jordan Brand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Brand "Jordan Brand") clothes and shoes, due to a sponsorship agreement. Bender had signed a similar agreement with his sponsor [Adidas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adidas "Adidas"), which prevented him to wear other brands.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-sneakers-56) Bender expressed disappointment in the [Croatian Basketball Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatian_Basketball_Federation "Croatian Basketball Federation")'s decision, even saying they had no reason to attack his loyalty to Croatia, or his family's loyalty to it.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-57) Adidas later designed a logo-less pair of shoes for Bender, in order for him to play with [Maccabi Tel Aviv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maccabi_Tel_Aviv_B.C. "Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C."), since they are also sponsored by Jordan Brand as well, as a response to the Croatian Basketball Federation's stance.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-58)

### Senior national team

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Senior national team")]

In June 2017, Bender was granted permission from the [Phoenix Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Suns "Phoenix Suns") to play for the senior [Croatian national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_men's_national_basketball_team "Croatia men's national basketball team") at [EuroBasket 2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EuroBasket_2017 "EuroBasket 2017").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-59) At EuroBasket 2017, he averaged 4.3 points, 2 rebounds, and 1 assist per game, in 6 games played.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-60)

## Player profile

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Player profile")]

Bender has been strongly compared to Kristaps Porziņģis to the point where NBA executives considered him a Top 5 selection similar to Porziņģis because of their playing styles, either due to it being a selling point or being a good cover overall.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-howard-61) However, while Porziņģis may be the stronger shooter and scorer, Bender is consistently labeled as the stronger passer and ball-handler.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-howard-61)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Bender's older brother, Ivan, played college basketball as a forward for the [Maryland Terrapins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland_Terrapins_men's_basketball "Maryland Terrapins men's basketball").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-62)

In order to learn the English language at a young age, Bender watched American sitcoms like _[Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friends "Friends")_ and _[The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fresh\_Prince\_of\_Bel-Air "The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air")_.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-63)

**Dragan Bender** (born 17 November 1997) is a Croatian former professional [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") player. He stands 7 ft 0 in (2.13 m) and played the [power forward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_forward_(basketball) "Power forward (basketball)") and [center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Center_(basketball) "Center (basketball)") positions. He was selected by the [Phoenix Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Suns "Phoenix Suns") with the fourth overall pick in the 2016 NBA draft but only played four years in the league. Bender represents the [Croatian national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_men's_national_basketball_team "Croatia men's national basketball team"), with experience in the [FIBA Europe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIBA_Europe "FIBA Europe") junior tournaments. Before playing in Israel, he competed with multiple teams in Croatia and in [Nikola Vujčić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikola_Vuj%C4%8Di%C4%87 "Nikola Vujčić")'s academy.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Bender was born on 17 November 1997, in [Čapljina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C4%8Capljina "Čapljina"), [Bosnia and Herzegovina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Bosnia and Herzegovina"), and he later moved to [Split, Croatia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Split,_Croatia "Split, Croatia").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-NBA_Draft-1) At 12 years of age, he started playing at [Nikola Vujčić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikola_Vuj%C4%8Di%C4%87 "Nikola Vujčić")'s basketball academy as a [point guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Point_guard "Point guard").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-jpost-2) Vujčić was a former [Maccabi Tel Aviv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maccabi_Tel_Aviv_B.C. "Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.") star and became Bender's guardian.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-br-3) At the academy, Bender became a more versatile player and he "learned how to play all the positions on the court."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-fastbreak-4) Bender played there along with his older brother, Ivan, with Bender also playing against guys that were Ivan's age when he first started playing.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-si-5) Bender also played with the [KK Split](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KK_Split "KK Split") youth teams at this time, and he appeared for the Croatian under-16 national basketball team.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-yahoo-6) He idolized and modeled his game after [Toni Kukoč](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toni_Kuko%C4%8D "Toni Kukoč"), a former Croatian [NBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA "NBA") player, while growing up and watched his old game tape.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-jpost-2) He mostly watched [EuroLeague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EuroLeague "EuroLeague") games but would sometimes tune into the NBA as well. One of his favorite EuroLeague players was [Šarūnas Jasikevičius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%A0ar%C5%ABnas_Jasikevi%C4%8Dius "Šarūnas Jasikevičius").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-si-5)

## Professional career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Professional career")]

### Split (2012–2013)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Split (2012–2013)")]

Bender made his professional debut at 15 years of age with [KK Split](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KK_Split "KK Split"). He played only a total of six minutes and added two points and one rebound.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-yahoo-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-eurobasket-7)

### Kaštela (2013–2014)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Kaštela (2013–2014)")]

For the following season, Bender remained in Croatia and signed with [KK Kaštela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KK_Ka%C5%A1tela "KK Kaštela"), who played in the country's second-best league.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-euroleague-8) With his help, the team was promoted to the [A-1 Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-1_Liga "A-1 Liga"), the top league in Croatia.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-kastela-9) Most notably, he made a game-winning shot with three seconds remaining against [KK Gorica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KK_Gorica "KK Gorica") to help his team secure the promotion.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-kastela-9) Later, in February 2014, Bender joined the [KK Cedevita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KK_Cedevita "KK Cedevita") junior team for the [Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Euroleague_Basketball_Next_Generation_Tournament "Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament"). He put up 21 points, 9 rebounds, and 6 assists vs the junior team of the Serbian club [KK Mega Basket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KK_Mega_Basket "KK Mega Basket").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-10)

### Ironi Ramat Gan (2014–2016)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Ironi Ramat Gan (2014–2016)")]

In 2014, Bender signed a seven-year contract with [Maccabi Tel Aviv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maccabi_Tel_Aviv_B.C. "Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C."), a team that played in the [Israeli Basketball Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Israeli_Basketball_Premier_League "Israeli Basketball Premier League") and the [EuroLeague](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EuroLeague "EuroLeague").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-future-11) He was soon [loaned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loan_(sports) "Loan (sports)") to [Ironi Ramat Gan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ironi_Ramat_Gan "Ironi Ramat Gan") of the [Liga Leumit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liga_Leumit_(basketball) "Liga Leumit (basketball)"), the second-tier-level league in Israel, for the 2014–15 season.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-12) He made his debut on 21 October 2014, posting 13 points, 13 rebounds, and 4 assists vs [Ramat HaSharon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.S._Ramat_HaSharon "A.S. Ramat HaSharon").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-13) He recorded another [double-double](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double-double_(basketball) "Double-double (basketball)") on 12 December, with 23 points and 12 rebounds in a win over [Maccabi Ra'anana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maccabi_Ra'anana "Maccabi Ra'anana").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-14) Bender scored a season-high 25 points as his team defeated [Barak Netanya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elitzur_Netanya_B.C. "Elitzur Netanya B.C.") by one point on 1 January 2015.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-15) After 28 games, he finished the season averaging 9.7 points, 7.4 rebounds, 2.6 assists, and 1.1 blocks.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-eurobasket-7) As the season came to a close, Bender returned to Maccabi Tel Aviv.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-16)

### Maccabi Tel Aviv (2015–2016)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Maccabi Tel Aviv (2015–2016)")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/88/Bender_BoxOut.JPG/250px-Bender_BoxOut.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bender_BoxOut.JPG)

Bender (#3) with Maccabi Tel Aviv in 2015

Bender debuted for Maccabi Tel Aviv in the Israeli Premier League on 11 October 2015, with 5 points, 3 rebounds, and 3 blocks in a win over [Maccabi Kiryat Gat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maccabi_Kiryat_Gat_B.C. "Maccabi Kiryat Gat B.C.").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-17) He scored double figures for the first time with the team in a rematch with Kiryat Gat, adding 15 points.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-yahoo-6)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-18) Bender scored a season-high 16 points on 31 December 2015, as his team defeated [Hapoel Holon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hapoel_Holon "Hapoel Holon").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-19) In 2015–16, he helped Maccabi Tel Aviv repeat as winners in the [2016 Israeli State Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Israeli_Basketball_State_Cup "2015–16 Israeli Basketball State Cup"), and he was named a foreign All-Star for the 2016 Israeli All-Star game.

On 6 April 2016, Bender declared for the 2016 NBA draft.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-20) His contract with Maccabi Tel Aviv was later bought out for $1.3 million.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-21)

### Phoenix Suns (2016–2019)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Phoenix Suns (2016–2019)")]

On 23 June 2016, Bender was selected by the [Phoenix Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Suns "Phoenix Suns") with the fourth overall pick in the 2016 NBA draft.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-22) He was widely billed as the best international prospect available in the draft, highly valued for his ability to shoot the ball in various ways as a big man, as well as his overall untapped potential in other facets of the game.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-23) As the fourth overall pick, Bender became the Suns' highest-selected rookie since [Armen Gilliam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armen_Gilliam "Armen Gilliam") was taken second overall in [1987](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1987_NBA_draft "1987 NBA draft"),[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-24) and the highest-selected Croatian to be taken in an NBA draft. On 7 July, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Suns and joined the team for the [2016 NBA Summer League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_NBA_Summer_League "2016 NBA Summer League").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-25) Bender made his debut for the Suns in their season opener on 26 October 2016, scoring 10 points on 4-of-5 shooting in a 113–94 loss to the [Sacramento Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacramento_Kings "Sacramento Kings").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-26) With Bender playing alongside [Devin Booker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devin_Booker "Devin Booker") and fellow rookie [Marquese Chriss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marquese_Chriss "Marquese Chriss"), the Suns became the first NBA team to get three teenagers on the floor in the same game.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-27) Bender also joined Booker and [Giannis Antetokounmpo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giannis_Antetokounmpo "Giannis Antetokounmpo") as the only 18-year-olds to score 10 points in a game since 2006–07.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-28) He had his second 10-point game of the season on 8 November in a 124–121 loss to the [Portland Trail Blazers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland_Trail_Blazers "Portland Trail Blazers").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-29) He then had his third 10-point game of the season on 3 December in a 138–109 loss to the [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_State_Warriors "Golden State Warriors").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-30) On 26 December, Bender recorded his first career double-double with season highs of 11 points and 13 rebounds in a 131–115 loss to the [Houston Rockets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Rockets "Houston Rockets").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-31) On 8 February 2017, Bender underwent a successful routine arthroscopic procedure on his right ankle to remove a bone spur. He was subsequently ruled out for approximately four to six weeks.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-32) He returned to action on 2 April 2017, against Houston.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-33)

In July 2017, Bender re-joined the Suns for the [2017 NBA Summer League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_NBA_Summer_League "2017 NBA Summer League").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-34) In five games, he averaged 14.2 points, 6.0 rebounds, and 2.4 assists per game. On 13 November 2017, Bender scored a career-high 15 points in a 100–93 loss to the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-35) On 16 December 2017, he set a new career high with 17 points in a 108–106 win over the [Minnesota Timberwolves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Timberwolves "Minnesota Timberwolves").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-36) On 7 January 2018, he scored 17 of his then career-high 20 points in the second half of the Suns' 114–100 win over the [Oklahoma City Thunder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma_City_Thunder "Oklahoma City Thunder"). He made a career-best six 3-pointers, going 5 of 6 in the second half.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-37) On 10 February 2018, he scored a career-high 23 points in a 123–113 loss to the [Denver Nuggets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Nuggets "Denver Nuggets").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-38) On 8 April 2018, Bender recorded 14 points and a career-high 14 rebounds in a 117–100 loss to the [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_State_Warriors "Golden State Warriors").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-39)

In July 2018, Bender re-joined the Suns for the [2018 NBA Summer League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_NBA_Summer_League "2018 NBA Summer League").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-40) On 30 October 2018, the Suns declined Bender's $5.9 million fourth year rookie option, making him a free agent after the season. On 5 April 2019, Bender recorded a career-high seven blocks in a 133–126 overtime win over the [New Orleans Pelicans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Pelicans "New Orleans Pelicans").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-41)

### Milwaukee Bucks (2019–2020)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Milwaukee Bucks (2019–2020)")]

In July 2019, Bender signed a two-year minimum deal with the [Milwaukee Bucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Bucks "Milwaukee Bucks").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-42) The first year of Bender's deal was partially guaranteed, but it became fully guaranteed when the Bucks did not waive Bender by 7 January, while the second is non-guaranteed.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-43) Bender was assigned to the [Wisconsin Herd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wisconsin_Herd "Wisconsin Herd") for the start of the [NBA G League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_G_League "NBA G League") season. On 10 February 2020, the [Milwaukee Bucks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee_Bucks "Milwaukee Bucks") announced that they had waived Bender.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-44)

### Golden State Warriors (2020)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Golden State Warriors (2020)")]

On 23 February 2020, the [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_State_Warriors "Golden State Warriors") announced that they had signed Bender to a 10-day contract.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-45) In his first game he played against his former team, the [Phoenix Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Suns "Phoenix Suns"), he recorded 13 points and 9 rebounds in a 115–99 win on 29 February.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-46) He then acquired a second 10-day contract on 5 March 2020. In his last game before the [NBA season was suspended](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suspension_of_the_2019%E2%80%9320_NBA_season "Suspension of the 2019–20 NBA season") due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_the_United_States "COVID-19 pandemic in the United States"), Bender tied his career high with 23 points on 8-of-12 shooting and added 7 rebounds in a 131–107 loss to the [Los Angeles Clippers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Clippers "Los Angeles Clippers") on 10 March.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-47) The season was suspended while Bender was still on contract, and he became a free agent before the season restarted in July.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-48) Bender's short and uneventful NBA career marked him as a high-profile draft bust.

### Maccabi Tel Aviv (2020–2021)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Maccabi Tel Aviv (2020–2021)")]

On 23 September 2020, Bender returned to the Israeli team [Maccabi Tel Aviv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maccabi_Tel_Aviv "Maccabi Tel Aviv").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-49) During the 2020–21 season, he averaged 6.6 points, 3.8 rebounds over 34 EuroLeague games. He suffered a season-ending injury in May 2021 that caused him to miss the entire 2021–22 season.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-50)

### Obradoiro (2022)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Obradoiro (2022)")]

On August 23, 2022, Bender signed with [Monbus Obradoiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obradoiro_CAB "Obradoiro CAB") of the Spanish [Liga ACB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liga_ACB "Liga ACB").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-51) On December 11, he suffered a [torn ACL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anterior_cruciate_ligament_injury "Anterior cruciate ligament injury") injury in his left knee and thus finished a season averaging 17.2 points and 6.6 rebounds on 52.7% shooting from the field in 10 games played for Obradoiro.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-aclinjury-2024update-52)

## National team career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: National team career")]

### Junior national team

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Junior national team")]

Bender competed for the Croatian national Under-16 team at the [2012 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_FIBA_Europe_Under-16_Championship "2012 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship"). in Latvia and Lithuania. Through five contests, he averaged 2.8 points and 1.4 rebounds in 5.6 minutes per game.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-53) The following year, he came back to the [2013 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013_FIBA_Europe_Under-16_Championship "2013 FIBA Europe Under-16 Championship") in Ukraine, improving through 9 games to 9.8 points, 10.8 rebounds and 4.1 assists in 35.4 minutes per game.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-54) Bender improved even further, while playing with the Croatian national Under-18 team, at the [2014 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_FIBA_Europe_Under-18_Championship "2014 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship") in Turkey. In 9 games, he averaged 14.4 points, 10.4 rebounds and 4.9 assists in 29 minutes per game, helping his team win the bronze medal, and being named to All-Tournament Team in the process.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-55)

In 2015, Bender was selected by Croatia for the [2015 FIBA Under-19 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_FIBA_Under-19_World_Championship "2015 FIBA Under-19 World Championship") in [Crete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crete "Crete"), Greece, but he was forced to withdraw because the team's players were obliged to wear [Jordan Brand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jordan_Brand "Jordan Brand") clothes and shoes, due to a sponsorship agreement. Bender had signed a similar agreement with his sponsor [Adidas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adidas "Adidas"), which prevented him to wear other brands.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-sneakers-56) Bender expressed disappointment in the [Croatian Basketball Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatian_Basketball_Federation "Croatian Basketball Federation")'s decision, even saying they had no reason to attack his loyalty to Croatia, or his family's loyalty to it.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-57) Adidas later designed a logo-less pair of shoes for Bender, in order for him to play with [Maccabi Tel Aviv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maccabi_Tel_Aviv_B.C. "Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C."), since they are also sponsored by Jordan Brand as well, as a response to the Croatian Basketball Federation's stance.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-58)

### Senior national team

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Senior national team")]

In June 2017, Bender was granted permission from the [Phoenix Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Suns "Phoenix Suns") to play for the senior [Croatian national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croatia_men's_national_basketball_team "Croatia men's national basketball team") at [EuroBasket 2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EuroBasket_2017 "EuroBasket 2017").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-59) At EuroBasket 2017, he averaged 4.3 points, 2 rebounds, and 1 assist per game, in 6 games played.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-60)

## Player profile

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Player profile")]

Bender has been strongly compared to Kristaps Porziņģis to the point where NBA executives considered him a Top 5 selection similar to Porziņģis because of their playing styles, either due to it being a selling point or being a good cover overall.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-howard-61) However, while Porziņģis may be the stronger shooter and scorer, Bender is consistently labeled as the stronger passer and ball-handler.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-howard-61)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Dragan_Bender&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Bender's older brother, Ivan, played college basketball as a forward for the [Maryland Terrapins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maryland_Terrapins_men's_basketball "Maryland Terrapins men's basketball").[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-62)

In order to learn the English language at a young age, Bender watched American sitcoms like _[Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friends "Friends")_ and _[The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Fresh\_Prince\_of\_Bel-Air "The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air")_.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragan_Bender#cite_note-63)

**Anthony Jermal Edwards** (born August 5, 2001), nicknamed "**Ant-Man**" or simply "**Ant**",[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Basketball-Reference.com-1) is an American professional [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") player for the [Minnesota Timberwolves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Timberwolves "Minnesota Timberwolves") of the [National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") (NBA). A [shooting guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shooting_guard "Shooting guard"), Edwards played [college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") for the [Georgia Bulldogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Bulldogs_basketball "Georgia Bulldogs basketball") and was selected with the [first overall pick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_first_overall_NBA_draft_picks "List of first overall NBA draft picks") by the Timberwolves in the [2020 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NBA_draft "2020 NBA draft"). He is a four-time [NBA All-Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NBA_All-Stars "List of NBA All-Stars"), a two-time [All-NBA Second Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-NBA_Second_Team "All-NBA Second Team") selection, and won a gold medal on the [2024 U.S. Olympic team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_men's_Olympic_basketball_team "2024 United States men's Olympic basketball team").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-2)

Edwards finished his high school career at [Holy Spirit Preparatory School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Spirit_Preparatory_School "Holy Spirit Preparatory School") in his hometown of [Atlanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta "Atlanta"), Georgia, where he was rated a consensus five-star [recruit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_recruiting "College recruiting") and one of the best players in the 2019 class by major recruiting services. As a senior, he earned [McDonald's All-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonald's_All-American_Game "McDonald's All-American Game") and [_USA Today_ All-USA first team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Today_All-USA_high_school_basketball_team "USA Today All-USA high school basketball team") honors. He committed to play college basketball for Georgia, becoming the highest-rated recruit to do so, and was named [SEC Freshman of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeastern_Conference_Men's_Basketball_Rookie_of_the_Year "Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year") after his freshman season with the team.

## Early life

Edwards spent his early life in [Oakland City, Atlanta, Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland_City,_Atlanta "Oakland City, Atlanta").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-3) When he was three years old, he was given the nickname "Ant-Man" by his father. For much of his childhood, Edwards played [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football") in the [running back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_back "Running back"), [quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback"), and [cornerback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornerback "Cornerback") positions.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-ROD-4) He played youth football for the Atlanta Vikings and became one of the best [Pop Warner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_Warner_Little_Scholars "Pop Warner Little Scholars") running backs in the country by age 10.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-ROD-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Jones-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Westerholm-6) Edwards switched his focus to basketball because he "thought it looked more fun" after watching his brothers play the sport. He often played basketball with his brothers at their grandmother's house. Entering ninth grade, he began training with Justin Holland, a former [college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") player for [Liberty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_Flames_basketball "Liberty Flames basketball") and an Atlanta-based basketball trainer.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-ROD-4)

## High school

Due to his success with the Atlanta Xpress 15-under [Amateur Athletic Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amateur_Athletic_Union "Amateur Athletic Union") team, Edwards was considered a four-star [recruit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_recruiting "College recruiting") by [Rivals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rivals.com "Rivals.com") in 2016.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-McDonald-7) He began playing high school basketball for [Therrell High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Therrell_High_School "Therrell High School") in Atlanta as a member of the 2019 class.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Krohn-8) In early January 2017, Edwards transferred to [Holy Spirit Preparatory School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Spirit_Preparatory_School "Holy Spirit Preparatory School") in Atlanta and [reclassified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reclassification_(education) "Reclassification (education)") to the 2020 class. He made the move in an effort to improve his academic performance, since Holy Spirit Preparatory had "small class sizes and support to help that."[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Neysmith-9)

[Rivals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rivals.com "Rivals.com"), Edwards was rated a five-star recruit, top-five player, and the top [shooting guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shooting_guard "Shooting guard") in the 2019 class.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Rivals-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-247Sports-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-ESPNr-20) basketball").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Krohn-8) He was drawn to Georgia because two of his favorite players, [Dwyane Wade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwyane_Wade "Dwyane Wade") and [Victor Oladipo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Oladipo "Victor Oladipo"), had been coached in college by head coach [Tom Crean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Crean_(basketball) "Tom Crean (basketball)").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-polacek-23)
