## College career

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6f/Anthony_Edwards_Georgia_2_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Anthony_Edwards_Georgia_2_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Anthony_Edwards_Georgia_2_(cropped).jpg)

Edwards in 2020

On November 5, 2019, Edwards made his debut for the Georgia Bulldogs, recording 24 points, 9 rebounds, and 4 steals in a 91–72 win over [Western Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Carolina_Catamounts_men's_basketball "Western Carolina Catamounts men's basketball"). It was the most points by a Georgia freshman debutant since [Basketball Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naismith_Memorial_Basketball_Hall_of_Fame "Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame") inductee [Dominique Wilkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominique_Wilkins "Dominique Wilkins") in 1979.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-24) On November 26, he scored a season-high 37 points, including 33 in the second half, and posted six rebounds, four steals, and three [blocks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Block_(basketball) "Block (basketball)") in a 93–85 loss to third-ranked [Michigan State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan_State_Spartans_men's_basketball "Michigan State Spartans men's basketball") at the [Maui Invitational](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Maui_Invitational_Tournament "2019 Maui Invitational Tournament"). Edwards became the first Georgia freshman to score at least 37 points in a game since [Jacky Dorsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacky_Dorsey "Jacky Dorsey") in 1975.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-msu-25) In his final game at the tournament, he led all scorers with 24 points and made the game-winning shot against [NCAA Division II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_II "NCAA Division II") team [Chaminade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaminade_Silverswords "Chaminade Silverswords").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-austin-26)

On February 1, 2020, Edwards recorded 29 points and 15 rebounds, both game-highs, in a 63–48 victory over [Texas A&M](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_A&M_Aggies_men's_basketball "Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-texasam-27) In his next game, he led all scorers with 32 points in an 81–75 loss to [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Gators_men's_basketball "Florida Gators men's basketball").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-florida-28) On February 26, Edwards scored 36 points and collected seven rebounds, four assists and four steals, in a 94–90 [overtime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports) "Overtime (sports)") defeat to [South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina_Gamecocks_men's_basketball "South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-29) As a freshman, he averaged 19.1 points, 5.2 rebounds and 2.8 assists per game.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-dortch-30) Edwards was the top scorer on his team and among freshmen nationally. He earned second-team All-SEC and [SEC Freshman of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeastern_Conference_Men's_Basketball_Rookie_of_the_Year "Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year") honors.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-SEC_awards-31) Edwards collected SEC Freshman of the Week accolades four times during the season, the most in program history.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-32) He was also one of five finalists for the [Jerry West Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_West_Award "Jerry West Award"), which recognizes the top collegiate [shooting guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shooting_guard "Shooting guard").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-33)

On March 20, 2020, in the spring of his freshman year, Edwards declared for the [2020 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NBA_draft "2020 NBA draft") as one of the most touted prospects in his class. He signed with an [agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_agent "Sports agent"), forgoing his remaining college basketball eligibility.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-declare-34)

## Professional career

### Minnesota Timberwolves (2020–present)

#### 2020–21 season: All-Rookie honors

The [2020 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NBA_draft "2020 NBA draft") was delayed by five months due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"). In November 2020, the [Minnesota Timberwolves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Timberwolves "Minnesota Timberwolves") selected Edwards as the No. 1 overall pick on draft night. On December 23, 2020, he made his NBA debut, putting up 15 points, 4 rebounds, and 4 assists in 25 minutes, in a 111–101 win against the [Detroit Pistons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Pistons "Detroit Pistons").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-35) On March 18, 2021, Edwards scored a then career-high 42 points, along with 7 rebounds and 3 assists, in a game against the [Phoenix Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Suns "Phoenix Suns"), becoming the third-youngest player to score 40+ points in NBA history.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-36) After the season, he finished second in [Rookie of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Rookie_of_the_Year_Award "NBA Rookie of the Year Award") voting and was named to the [NBA All-Rookie First Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_All-Rookie_First_Team "NBA All-Rookie First Team").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-38)

#### 2021–22 season: First playoff appearance

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Anthony_Edwards_Kentavious_Caldwell-Pope_%2851734745028%29_%28cropped%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Anthony_Edwards_Kentavious_Caldwell-Pope_%2851734745028%29_%28cropped%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Anthony_Edwards_Kentavious_Caldwell-Pope_(51734745028)_(cropped)_(cropped).jpg)

Edwards in 2021

On November 10, 2021, Edwards scored a then career-high 48 points on 7 three-pointers in a 123–110 loss to the [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_State_Warriors "Golden State Warriors").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-39) On December 15, Edwards had 38 points and a franchise record 10 three-pointers in a 124–107 win over the [Denver Nuggets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Nuggets "Denver Nuggets"). He became the youngest NBA player ever with 10 three-pointers in a game, breaking the previous record set in 2015 by [Kyrie Irving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyrie_Irving "Kyrie Irving") at age 22. Edwards also reached 2,000 career points in fewer games than any player in franchise history.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-40) On January 25, 2022, in a 109–107 win over the [Portland Trail Blazers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland_Trail_Blazers "Portland Trail Blazers"), he became the first player in NBA history to record a stat line of at least 40 points, 9 rebounds, 3 blocks, 3 steals, and 5 three-pointers in a single game; he joined [Carmelo Anthony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmelo_Anthony "Carmelo Anthony") as the only players to score 40 points without an assist at 20 years old or younger.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-42) On April 7, 2022, Edwards scored a then career-high 49 points in a 127–121 win over the [San Antonio Spurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Antonio_Spurs "San Antonio Spurs").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-43)

In his playoff debut on April 16, 2022, he logged 36 points and 6 assists in a 130–117 Game 1 win over the [Memphis Grizzlies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis_Grizzlies "Memphis Grizzlies") in the opening round of the [2022 NBA playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NBA_playoffs "2022 NBA playoffs").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-44) Minnesota lost to Memphis despite Edwards's 30-point, 5-rebound, 5-assist, 2-steal and 2-block outing in the 114–106 close-out loss in Game 6.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-45)

#### 2022–23 season: First All-Star appearance

On January 21, 2023, Edwards scored a season-high 44 points, including a season-high 8 three-pointers, along with 6 rebounds, 4 assists, 3 steals, and 3 blocks in a 113–104 win over the [Houston Rockets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Rockets "Houston Rockets").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-46) On February 10, 2023, he was named an [All-Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_All-Star "NBA All-Star") for the first time in his career as a reserve. Edwards and [De'Aaron Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De'Aaron_Fox "De'Aaron Fox") were announced as injury replacements for injured stars [Stephen Curry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Curry "Stephen Curry") and [Zion Williamson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zion_Williamson "Zion Williamson").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-47) On April 9, in the final game of the [2022–23 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NBA_season "2022–23 NBA season"), Edwards recorded 26 points, 13 rebounds, 4 assists, 4 steals, and 4 blocks to help lead the Timberwolves to a 113–108 win over the [New Orleans Pelicans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Pelicans "New Orleans Pelicans"), earning the eight seed in the Western Conference play-in tournament.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-48)

In Game 2 of the Timberwolves' first-round playoff series against the [Denver Nuggets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Nuggets "Denver Nuggets"), Edwards put up 41 points in a 122–113 loss. His 41 points also set a Timberwolves franchise record for the most points scored in a playoff game, surpassing [Sam Cassell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Cassell "Sam Cassell")'s previous record of 40.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-49) On April 21, in Game 3 of the first round of the playoffs, Edwards scored 36 points in a 120–111 loss. He joined [Kobe Bryant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kobe_Bryant "Kobe Bryant") with the second-most 30-point NBA playoff games before turning 22 years old.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-50) In Game 4, Edwards had 34 points, 6 rebounds, 5 assists, 2 steals, and 3 blocks and scored a crucial 3-pointer to lead the Timberwolves to a 114–108 overtime win.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-51) In Game 5, the Timberwolves were eliminated from the playoffs by the [eventual NBA champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NBA_Finals "2023 NBA Finals") Nuggets despite 29 points, 8 rebounds, 7 assists, and 2 blocks by Edwards. With the Nuggets leading 112–109 in the final seconds of the game, Edwards missed a game-tying three-pointer at the buzzer.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-52)

#### 2023–24 season: First All-NBA appearance

Edwards changed his jersey number from #1 to #5 before the 2023–24 season.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-53) On November 13, 2023, he was named the NBA Western Conference Player of the Week for the first time in his career after leading Minnesota to an undefeated week (4–0) with averages of 31.3 points, 6.3 rebounds, 6.8 assists and 2.0 steals.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-54) On January 27, 2024, Edwards recorded 32 points, 6 rebounds and a career-high 12 assists in a 113–112 loss against the [San Antonio Spurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Antonio_Spurs "San Antonio Spurs").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-55) On February 1, Edwards was named to his second [All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_All-Star_Game "2024 NBA All-Star Game") as a Western Conference reserve.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-56) On April 9, Edwards put up a then career-high 51 points in a 130–121 win over the [Washington Wizards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Wizards "Washington Wizards").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-57) At the season's end, Edwards was named to the [All-NBA Second Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-NBA_Team "All-NBA Team") for the first time in his career.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-58)

In Game 4 of the [first round of the playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_playoffs#(3)_Minnesota_Timberwolves_vs._(6)_Phoenix_Suns "2024 NBA playoffs") against Phoenix, Edwards scored 31 of his 40 points in the second half, along with nine rebounds and six assists in a 122–116 win to close out the series. It was the Timberwolves' first playoff series win in 20 years. He also surpassed [Kevin Garnett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Garnett "Kevin Garnett") for the most 30-point playoff games in Timberwolves franchise history, with eight.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-60) In Game 1 of the [Western Conference Semifinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_playoffs#(2)_Denver_Nuggets_vs._(3)_Minnesota_Timberwolves "2024 NBA playoffs"), Edwards scored a then playoff career-high and franchise postseason-record 43 points in a 106–99 victory over the Nuggets. He joined [Kobe Bryant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kobe_Bryant "Kobe Bryant") as the only players with consecutive 40-point games at age 22 or younger in NBA postseason history.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-61) In Game 4 of the Western Conference Semifinals, Edwards scored a playoff career-high and franchise postseason-record 44 points, along with five rebounds and five assists, in a 115–107 loss to the Nuggets.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-62) In Game 4 of the [Western Conference Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_playoffs#(3)_Minnesota_Timberwolves_vs._(5)_Dallas_Mavericks "2024 NBA playoffs"), Edwards posted a near triple-double with 29 points, 10 rebounds and 9 assists in a 105–100 victory over the [Dallas Mavericks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Mavericks "Dallas Mavericks").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-63) Minnesota would go on to lose to Dallas in five games despite Edwards 28-point, 9-rebound and 6-assist outing in a 124–103 close-out loss in Game 5.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-64)

#### 2024–25 season: Three-point scoring leader

On January 4, 2025, Edwards scored a then career-high 53 points and tied his career-high with 10 three-pointers in a 119–105 loss to the [Detroit Pistons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Pistons "Detroit Pistons").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-65) On January 25, Edwards surpassed [Karl-Anthony Towns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns "Karl-Anthony Towns") for the most career three-pointers in Timberwolves franchise history with 976, in a 133–104 win over the [Denver Nuggets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Nuggets "Denver Nuggets").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-66) On January 30, Edwards was named to his third [All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_NBA_All-Star_Game "2025 NBA All-Star Game") in a row as a Western Conference reserve.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-67) On February 5, Edwards recorded 49 points (20 in the third quarter) and 9 rebounds in a 127–109 win over the [Chicago Bulls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bulls "Chicago Bulls"). He tied [Kevin Garnett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Garnett "Kevin Garnett") for the second-most 30-point games and tied Karl-Anthony Towns for the most 40-point games in team history.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-68) The next day, Edwards had 41 points, seven rebounds and six assists in a 127–114 win over the [Houston Rockets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Rockets "Houston Rockets"). It was Edwards’ 14th career 40-point game, passing Towns (13) for the most in franchise history. He became just the third player in Minnesota history to tally back-to-back 40-point games, joining [Andrew Wiggins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Wiggins "Andrew Wiggins") (2017) and [Kevin Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Love "Kevin Love") (2014). He also broke the record for the youngest player in NBA history to reach 1,000 career three-point baskets (23y, 185d).[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-:0-69)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-71) On February 10, Edwards put up 44 points in a 128–107 loss to the [Cleveland Cavaliers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Cavaliers "Cleveland Cavaliers"). He became the first player in Timberwolves franchise history to achieve at least three consecutive 40-point games.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-72) On April 10, Edwards scored 44 points, including 18 during Minnesota's franchise-record, 52-point third quarter, and the Timberwolves beat the [Memphis Grizzlies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis_Grizzlies "Memphis Grizzlies") 141–125.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-73) At the end of the season, Edwards became the three-point scoring leader (320 3-pointers made). It was the first time in Edwards’ career that he reached 300 made 3s. It’s also the seventh-highest total in NBA history.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-74) He also finished third in the [NBA Clutch Player of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Clutch_Player_of_the_Year "NBA Clutch Player of the Year") voting.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-75)

On April 27, in Game 4 of the first round of the playoffs, Edwards scored 43 points to go along with nine rebounds and six assists in a 116–113 win over the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers").[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-76) On May 6, in Game 1 of the second round, Edwards recorded 23 points and a playoff career-high 14 rebounds in a 99–88 loss against the [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_State_Warriors "Golden State Warriors").[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-77) On May 14, in Game 5, Edwards had 22 points, 7 rebounds, and a playoff career-high 12 assists in a 121–110 closeout victory over the Warriors, guiding the Timberwolves to their second consecutive [Western Conference Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_NBA_playoffs#(1)_Oklahoma_City_Thunder_vs._(6)_Minnesota_Timberwolves "2025 NBA playoffs").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-78) On May 24, In Game 3 of the Western Conference Finals, Edwards tallied 30 points, nine rebounds and six assists in just three quarters, leading the Timberwolves to a 143–101 blowout win over the [Oklahoma City Thunder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma_City_Thunder "Oklahoma City Thunder"). The victory cut the Thunder’s series lead to 2–1 and marked the Timberwolves’ highest-scoring playoff game in franchise history.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-79) Minnesota went on to lose to Oklahoma City in five games.

#### 2025–26 season: All-Star Game MVP

On November 30, 2025, Edwards scored 32 points in a 125–112 win over the [San Antonio Spurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Antonio_Spurs "San Antonio Spurs"), marking his 102nd career 30-point game and setting a new Timberwolves franchise record.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-80)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-81) On December 2, Edwards scored a season-high 44 points to lead the Timberwolves to a 149–142 overtime victory over the [New Orleans Pelicans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_New_Orleans_Pelicans_season "2025–26 New Orleans Pelicans season"). He poured in 34 of those 44 points in the second half, including a driving layup with 2.3 seconds remaining in regulation that forced overtime.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-82)

On January 8, 2026, Edwards recorded 25 points, seven rebounds, and nine assists in a 131–122 win over the [Cleveland Cavaliers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_Cleveland_Cavaliers_season "2025–26 Cleveland Cavaliers season"). With the performance, he became the seventh player in NBA history to reach 10,000 career points before turning 25, joining [Kobe Bryant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kobe_Bryant "Kobe Bryant"), [Tracy McGrady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracy_McGrady "Tracy McGrady"), [LeBron James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeBron_James "LeBron James"), [Carmelo Anthony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmelo_Anthony "Carmelo Anthony"), [Kevin Durant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Durant "Kevin Durant"), and [Luka Dončić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Don%C4%8Di%C4%87 "Luka Dončić"). Edwards also became the third-youngest player in NBA history to reach 10,000 career points, trailing only LeBron James and Kevin Durant.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-83)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-84) On January 17, Edwards scored a career-high 55 points, including 26 in the fourth quarter, in a 126–123 loss to the [San Antonio Spurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_San_Antonio_Spurs_season "2025–26 San Antonio Spurs season").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-85)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-86) On February 1, Edwards was named to his fourth [All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_NBA_All-Star_Game "2026 NBA All-Star Game") in a row as a Western Conference reserve.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-87) He was named the [NBA All-Star Game MVP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_All-Star_Game_Most_Valuable_Player "NBA All-Star Game Most Valuable Player") after recording a total of 32 points and 9 rebounds in 26 minutes across 3 games for the USA Stars.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-88) On February 3, Edwards posted 41 points, six rebounds, six assists and five steals, while knocking down seven three-pointers, leading the Timberwolves to a 117–110 win over the [Memphis Grizzlies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis_Grizzlies "Memphis Grizzlies"). In doing so, he became the first player in franchise history to record at least 40 points, five steals and five made three-pointers in a single game.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-89)

On May 10, in Game 4 of the [Western Conference Semifinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_NBA_playoffs#(2)_San_Antonio_Spurs_vs._(6)_Minnesota_Timberwolves "2026 NBA playoffs"), Edwards scored 36 points in a 114–109 victory over the [San Antonio Spurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_San_Antonio_Spurs_season "2025–26 San Antonio Spurs season") to tie the series at 2–2. In the process, Edwards recorded his 18th career playoff game with 30 or more points before turning 25, tying [Dwyane Wade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwyane_Wade "Dwyane Wade") for the fourth-most in NBA history. Ahead of him are LeBron James (30), Kobe Bryant (26), and Kevin Durant (22).[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-90) Minnesota went on to lose to San Antonio in six games.

## National team career

Edwards was a member of the [United States national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_men's_national_basketball_team "United States men's national basketball team") that competed in the [2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_United_States_FIBA_Basketball_World_Cup_team "2023 United States FIBA Basketball World Cup team"). He started all eight games and was selected in the [All-FIBA World Cup Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIBA_Basketball_World_Cup_All-Tournament_Team "FIBA Basketball World Cup All-Tournament Team"). He was the leading scorer for the U.S., averaging 18.9 points per game. The team finished in fourth place.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-91) He was named to the [2024 Olympic team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_men's_Olympic_basketball_team "2024 United States men's Olympic basketball team").[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-92) He helped Team USA win the gold medal, and in six games, he averaged 12.8 points, 2.8 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 1.3 steals per game while shooting 58% from the field.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-93)

## Player profile

Edwards plays primarily as a shooting guard. He is listed at 6 feet 4 inches (1.93 m) and weighs 225lb (102 kilograms).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Basketball-Reference.com-1) He’s known for his explosive athleticism, often going viral for his thunderous [poster dunks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posterized "Posterized"), including one over [John Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Collins_(basketball) "John Collins (basketball)") that the NBA named the 2023–24 Dunk of the Year.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-94)[The Ringer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ringer_(website) "The Ringer (website)") called him "a preposterous athlete with a nice jumper and better instincts".[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-95) He’s drawn comparisons to a young [Michael Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jordan "Michael Jordan") for his ability to finish around the rim. “They have a lot of the same mannerisms. The moves, the fadeaway, the athleticism, the poster dunks… that same kind of work ethic, that same kind of ‘I don’t sleep at all at night because I’m ready to play, I’m ready to hoop,” according to teammate [Mike Conley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Conley_Jr. "Mike Conley Jr.").[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-96)

Despite pre-draft concerns that he was a limited long-range scorer, Edwards has developed an efficient, high-volume three-point shot — shooting 37% on eight attempts per game.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Basketball-Reference.com-1) He led the NBA in three-pointers made for the 2024–25 season.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-97) The same year, he became the youngest player in NBA history to make 1,000 threes.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-:0-69)

His stout frame, lateral speed and competitiveness have helped transform his reputation on the defensive end — [Team USA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_men's_national_basketball_team "United States men's national basketball team") coach [Steve Kerr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Kerr "Steve Kerr") called his on-ball defense “amazing” during the FIBA World Cup.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-98) His ability to match up against both long wings and shifty guards has garnered praise from Timberwolves head coach [Chris Finch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Finch "Chris Finch"). Edwards himself believes his defense is “overlooked” by the national media.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-99) In 2024, he won the NBA Fan Favorite award for Block of Year after leaping to prevent a game-winning shot by the [Pacers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana_Pacers "Indiana Pacers")' [Aaron Nesmith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Nesmith "Aaron Nesmith").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-100)

## Personal life

Edwards's daughter, Aislynn, was born in March 2024.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-102) Edwards left the Timberwolves' March 1 game against the [Sacramento Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacramento_Kings "Sacramento Kings") at halftime to be with Aislynn's mother, Shannon Jackson, as their child was born.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-103) Edwards and Jackson got married on July 16, 2026.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-104)[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-105)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-106) Including Aislynn, Edwards reportedly has four children with four different women.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-107)

Edwards's mother, Yvette, and grandmother, Shirley, both died of cancer during an eight-month span in 2015, when he was in eighth grade. He has worn the No. 5 basketball jersey since high school to honor them, as they both died on the fifth day of the month.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-selfmade-108) After their deaths, Edwards was raised by his sister, Antoinette, and brother, Antoine, who shared [legal custody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Child_custody "Child custody") of him.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Towers-109) In high school, Edwards frequently worked as an instructor at youth camps.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Pourtout-110) He intended to major in [marketing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marketing "Marketing") while attending the [University of Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Georgia "University of Georgia").[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-bio-111)

During his childhood, Edwards also starred in baseball, often acting as his team's fourth or fifth hitter in the batting order. He has jokingly said he was very skilled at a variety of sports when he was younger. He owns two [dogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dog "Dog") and has also expressed his affinity for [lions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lion "Lion"), although he does not believe he has the requisite space to care for one.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-112)

Edwards made his acting debut in the 2022 sports drama film _[Hustle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hustle\_(2022\_film) "Hustle (2022 film)")._[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-113)

In 2023, [Adidas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adidas "Adidas") released the AE1, his first signature shoe. It quickly became a best-seller, prompting the company to sign him to a multiyear extension worth "around $50 million".[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-114)

### Controversies

In September 2022, Edwards posted a video to his Instagram story referring to a group of shirtless men standing on a sidewalk with a homophobic slur.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-115) The NBA fined him $40,000 for using "offensive and derogatory language."[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-116)

In December 2023, Paige Jordae, an [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram") model, accused Edwards of impregnating her and then offering her $100,000 to get an abortion.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-117) Jordae posted screenshots of text messages with Edwards.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-118) The screenshots, which were initially posted to Jordae's Instagram story, also included a screenshot of a pending wire transfer of $100,000 on November 27, 2023.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-119) Edwards responded, "I am handling my personal matters privately and will not be commenting on them any further at this time."[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-120)

**Anthony Jermal Edwards** (born August 5, 2001), nicknamed "**Ant-Man**" or simply "**Ant**",[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Basketball-Reference.com-1) is an American professional [basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") player for the [Minnesota Timberwolves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Timberwolves "Minnesota Timberwolves") of the [National Basketball Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") (NBA). A [shooting guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shooting_guard "Shooting guard"), Edwards played [college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") for the [Georgia Bulldogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Bulldogs_basketball "Georgia Bulldogs basketball") and was selected with the [first overall pick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_first_overall_NBA_draft_picks "List of first overall NBA draft picks") by the Timberwolves in the [2020 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NBA_draft "2020 NBA draft"). He is a four-time [NBA All-Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_NBA_All-Stars "List of NBA All-Stars"), a two-time [All-NBA Second Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-NBA_Second_Team "All-NBA Second Team") selection, and won a gold medal on the [2024 U.S. Olympic team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_men's_Olympic_basketball_team "2024 United States men's Olympic basketball team").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-2)

Edwards finished his high school career at [Holy Spirit Preparatory School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Spirit_Preparatory_School "Holy Spirit Preparatory School") in his hometown of [Atlanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta "Atlanta"), Georgia, where he was rated a consensus five-star [recruit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_recruiting "College recruiting") and one of the best players in the 2019 class by major recruiting services. As a senior, he earned [McDonald's All-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonald's_All-American_Game "McDonald's All-American Game") and [_USA Today_ All-USA first team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA_Today_All-USA_high_school_basketball_team "USA Today All-USA high school basketball team") honors. He committed to play college basketball for Georgia, becoming the highest-rated recruit to do so, and was named [SEC Freshman of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeastern_Conference_Men's_Basketball_Rookie_of_the_Year "Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year") after his freshman season with the team.

## Early life

Edwards spent his early life in [Oakland City, Atlanta, Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oakland_City,_Atlanta "Oakland City, Atlanta").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-3) When he was three years old, he was given the nickname "Ant-Man" by his father. For much of his childhood, Edwards played [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football") in the [running back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Running_back "Running back"), [quarterback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quarterback "Quarterback"), and [cornerback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornerback "Cornerback") positions.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-ROD-4) He played youth football for the Atlanta Vikings and became one of the best [Pop Warner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_Warner_Little_Scholars "Pop Warner Little Scholars") running backs in the country by age 10.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-ROD-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Jones-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Westerholm-6) Edwards switched his focus to basketball because he "thought it looked more fun" after watching his brothers play the sport. He often played basketball with his brothers at their grandmother's house. Entering ninth grade, he began training with Justin Holland, a former [college basketball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") player for [Liberty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_Flames_basketball "Liberty Flames basketball") and an Atlanta-based basketball trainer.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-ROD-4)

## High school

Due to his success with the Atlanta Xpress 15-under [Amateur Athletic Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amateur_Athletic_Union "Amateur Athletic Union") team, Edwards was considered a four-star [recruit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_recruiting "College recruiting") by [Rivals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rivals.com "Rivals.com") in 2016.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-McDonald-7) He began playing high school basketball for [Therrell High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Therrell_High_School "Therrell High School") in Atlanta as a member of the 2019 class.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Krohn-8) In early January 2017, Edwards transferred to [Holy Spirit Preparatory School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Spirit_Preparatory_School "Holy Spirit Preparatory School") in Atlanta and [reclassified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reclassification_(education) "Reclassification (education)") to the 2020 class. He made the move in an effort to improve his academic performance, since Holy Spirit Preparatory had "small class sizes and support to help that."[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Neysmith-9)

[Georgia Independent School Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Independent_School_Association "Georgia Independent School Association") (GISA) Class AAA state championship.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Bulletin-10) He reclassified back to the 2019 class in November 2018 after seeing academic improvement.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Krohn-8)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-11) As a result, Edwards rose ### Recruiting

By consensus among major recruiting services [247Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/247Sports "247Sports"), [ESPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESPN "ESPN"), and [Rivals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rivals.com "Rivals.com"), Edwards was rated a five-star recruit, top-five player, and the top [shooting guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shooting_guard "Shooting guard") in the 2019 class.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Rivals-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-247Sports-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-ESPNr-20) On February 11, 2019, he committed to play college basketball for [Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgia_Bulldogs_men's_basketball "Georgia Bulldogs men's basketball"), becoming the program's best recruit in the modern recruiting era.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-22) Edwards chose the Bulldogs over offers from [Florida State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_State_Seminoles_men's_basketball "Florida State Seminoles men's basketball"), [Kansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kansas_Jayhawks_men's_basketball "Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball"), [Kentucky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kentucky_Wildcats_men's_basketball "Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball"), and [North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina_Tar_Heels_men's_basketball "North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Krohn-8) He was drawn to Georgia because two of his favorite players, [Dwyane Wade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwyane_Wade "Dwyane Wade") and [Victor Oladipo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor_Oladipo "Victor Oladipo"), had been coached in college by head coach [Tom Crean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Crean_(basketball) "Tom Crean (basketball)").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-polacek-23)

## College career

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6f/Anthony_Edwards_Georgia_2_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Anthony_Edwards_Georgia_2_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Anthony_Edwards_Georgia_2_(cropped).jpg)

Edwards in 2020

On November 5, 2019, Edwards made his debut for the Georgia Bulldogs, recording 24 points, 9 rebounds, and 4 steals in a 91–72 win over [Western Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Carolina_Catamounts_men's_basketball "Western Carolina Catamounts men's basketball"). It was the most points by a Georgia freshman debutant since [Basketball Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naismith_Memorial_Basketball_Hall_of_Fame "Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame") inductee [Dominique Wilkins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominique_Wilkins "Dominique Wilkins") in 1979.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-24) On November 26, he scored a season-high 37 points, including 33 in the second half, and posted six rebounds, four steals, and three [blocks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Block_(basketball) "Block (basketball)") in a 93–85 loss to third-ranked [Michigan State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan_State_Spartans_men's_basketball "Michigan State Spartans men's basketball") at the [Maui Invitational](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Maui_Invitational_Tournament "2019 Maui Invitational Tournament"). Edwards became the first Georgia freshman to score at least 37 points in a game since [Jacky Dorsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacky_Dorsey "Jacky Dorsey") in 1975.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-msu-25) In his final game at the tournament, he led all scorers with 24 points and made the game-winning shot against [NCAA Division II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NCAA_Division_II "NCAA Division II") team [Chaminade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaminade_Silverswords "Chaminade Silverswords").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-austin-26)

On February 1, 2020, Edwards recorded 29 points and 15 rebounds, both game-highs, in a 63–48 victory over [Texas A&M](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_A&M_Aggies_men's_basketball "Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-texasam-27) In his next game, he led all scorers with 32 points in an 81–75 loss to [Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_Gators_men's_basketball "Florida Gators men's basketball").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-florida-28) On February 26, Edwards scored 36 points and collected seven rebounds, four assists and four steals, in a 94–90 [overtime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports) "Overtime (sports)") defeat to [South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Carolina_Gamecocks_men's_basketball "South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-29) As a freshman, he averaged 19.1 points, 5.2 rebounds and 2.8 assists per game.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-dortch-30) Edwards was the top scorer on his team and among freshmen nationally. He earned second-team All-SEC and [SEC Freshman of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeastern_Conference_Men's_Basketball_Rookie_of_the_Year "Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year") honors.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-SEC_awards-31) Edwards collected SEC Freshman of the Week accolades four times during the season, the most in program history.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-32) He was also one of five finalists for the [Jerry West Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_West_Award "Jerry West Award"), which recognizes the top collegiate [shooting guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shooting_guard "Shooting guard").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-33)

On March 20, 2020, in the spring of his freshman year, Edwards declared for the [2020 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NBA_draft "2020 NBA draft") as one of the most touted prospects in his class. He signed with an [agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_agent "Sports agent"), forgoing his remaining college basketball eligibility.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-declare-34)

## Professional career

### Minnesota Timberwolves (2020–present)

#### 2020–21 season: All-Rookie honors

The [2020 NBA draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_NBA_draft "2020 NBA draft") was delayed by five months due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"). In November 2020, the [Minnesota Timberwolves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minnesota_Timberwolves "Minnesota Timberwolves") selected Edwards as the No. 1 overall pick on draft night. On December 23, 2020, he made his NBA debut, putting up 15 points, 4 rebounds, and 4 assists in 25 minutes, in a 111–101 win against the [Detroit Pistons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Pistons "Detroit Pistons").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-35) On March 18, 2021, Edwards scored a then career-high 42 points, along with 7 rebounds and 3 assists, in a game against the [Phoenix Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoenix_Suns "Phoenix Suns"), becoming the third-youngest player to score 40+ points in NBA history.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-36) After the season, he finished second in [Rookie of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Rookie_of_the_Year_Award "NBA Rookie of the Year Award") voting and was named to the [NBA All-Rookie First Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_All-Rookie_First_Team "NBA All-Rookie First Team").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-38)

#### 2021–22 season: First playoff appearance

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/Anthony_Edwards_Kentavious_Caldwell-Pope_%2851734745028%29_%28cropped%29_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Anthony_Edwards_Kentavious_Caldwell-Pope_%2851734745028%29_%28cropped%29_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Anthony_Edwards_Kentavious_Caldwell-Pope_(51734745028)_(cropped)_(cropped).jpg)

Edwards in 2021

On November 10, 2021, Edwards scored a then career-high 48 points on 7 three-pointers in a 123–110 loss to the [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_State_Warriors "Golden State Warriors").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-39) On December 15, Edwards had 38 points and a franchise record 10 three-pointers in a 124–107 win over the [Denver Nuggets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Nuggets "Denver Nuggets"). He became the youngest NBA player ever with 10 three-pointers in a game, breaking the previous record set in 2015 by [Kyrie Irving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyrie_Irving "Kyrie Irving") at age 22. Edwards also reached 2,000 career points in fewer games than any player in franchise history.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-40) On January 25, 2022, in a 109–107 win over the [Portland Trail Blazers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland_Trail_Blazers "Portland Trail Blazers"), he became the first player in NBA history to record a stat line of at least 40 points, 9 rebounds, 3 blocks, 3 steals, and 5 three-pointers in a single game; he joined [Carmelo Anthony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmelo_Anthony "Carmelo Anthony") as the only players to score 40 points without an assist at 20 years old or younger.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-42) On April 7, 2022, Edwards scored a then career-high 49 points in a 127–121 win over the [San Antonio Spurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Antonio_Spurs "San Antonio Spurs").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-43)

In his playoff debut on April 16, 2022, he logged 36 points and 6 assists in a 130–117 Game 1 win over the [Memphis Grizzlies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis_Grizzlies "Memphis Grizzlies") in the opening round of the [2022 NBA playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_NBA_playoffs "2022 NBA playoffs").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-44) Minnesota lost to Memphis despite Edwards's 30-point, 5-rebound, 5-assist, 2-steal and 2-block outing in the 114–106 close-out loss in Game 6.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-45)

#### 2022–23 season: First All-Star appearance

On January 21, 2023, Edwards scored a season-high 44 points, including a season-high 8 three-pointers, along with 6 rebounds, 4 assists, 3 steals, and 3 blocks in a 113–104 win over the [Houston Rockets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Rockets "Houston Rockets").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-46) On February 10, 2023, he was named an [All-Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_All-Star "NBA All-Star") for the first time in his career as a reserve. Edwards and [De'Aaron Fox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/De'Aaron_Fox "De'Aaron Fox") were announced as injury replacements for injured stars [Stephen Curry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Curry "Stephen Curry") and [Zion Williamson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zion_Williamson "Zion Williamson").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-47) On April 9, in the final game of the [2022–23 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022%E2%80%9323_NBA_season "2022–23 NBA season"), Edwards recorded 26 points, 13 rebounds, 4 assists, 4 steals, and 4 blocks to help lead the Timberwolves to a 113–108 win over the [New Orleans Pelicans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Orleans_Pelicans "New Orleans Pelicans"), earning the eight seed in the Western Conference play-in tournament.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-48)

In Game 2 of the Timberwolves' first-round playoff series against the [Denver Nuggets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Nuggets "Denver Nuggets"), Edwards put up 41 points in a 122–113 loss. His 41 points also set a Timberwolves franchise record for the most points scored in a playoff game, surpassing [Sam Cassell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Cassell "Sam Cassell")'s previous record of 40.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-49) On April 21, in Game 3 of the first round of the playoffs, Edwards scored 36 points in a 120–111 loss. He joined [Kobe Bryant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kobe_Bryant "Kobe Bryant") with the second-most 30-point NBA playoff games before turning 22 years old.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-50) In Game 4, Edwards had 34 points, 6 rebounds, 5 assists, 2 steals, and 3 blocks and scored a crucial 3-pointer to lead the Timberwolves to a 114–108 overtime win.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-51) In Game 5, the Timberwolves were eliminated from the playoffs by the [eventual NBA champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_NBA_Finals "2023 NBA Finals") Nuggets despite 29 points, 8 rebounds, 7 assists, and 2 blocks by Edwards. With the Nuggets leading 112–109 in the final seconds of the game, Edwards missed a game-tying three-pointer at the buzzer.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-52)

#### 2023–24 season: First All-NBA appearance

Edwards changed his jersey number from #1 to #5 before the 2023–24 season.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-53) On November 13, 2023, he was named the NBA Western Conference Player of the Week for the first time in his career after leading Minnesota to an undefeated week (4–0) with averages of 31.3 points, 6.3 rebounds, 6.8 assists and 2.0 steals.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-54) On January 27, 2024, Edwards recorded 32 points, 6 rebounds and a career-high 12 assists in a 113–112 loss against the [San Antonio Spurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Antonio_Spurs "San Antonio Spurs").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-55) On February 1, Edwards was named to his second [All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_All-Star_Game "2024 NBA All-Star Game") as a Western Conference reserve.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-56) On April 9, Edwards put up a then career-high 51 points in a 130–121 win over the [Washington Wizards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Wizards "Washington Wizards").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-57) At the season's end, Edwards was named to the [All-NBA Second Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All-NBA_Team "All-NBA Team") for the first time in his career.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-58)

In Game 4 of the [first round of the playoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_playoffs#(3)_Minnesota_Timberwolves_vs._(6)_Phoenix_Suns "2024 NBA playoffs") against Phoenix, Edwards scored 31 of his 40 points in the second half, along with nine rebounds and six assists in a 122–116 win to close out the series. It was the Timberwolves' first playoff series win in 20 years. He also surpassed [Kevin Garnett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Garnett "Kevin Garnett") for the most 30-point playoff games in Timberwolves franchise history, with eight.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-60) In Game 1 of the [Western Conference Semifinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_playoffs#(2)_Denver_Nuggets_vs._(3)_Minnesota_Timberwolves "2024 NBA playoffs"), Edwards scored a then playoff career-high and franchise postseason-record 43 points in a 106–99 victory over the Nuggets. He joined [Kobe Bryant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kobe_Bryant "Kobe Bryant") as the only players with consecutive 40-point games at age 22 or younger in NBA postseason history.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-61) In Game 4 of the Western Conference Semifinals, Edwards scored a playoff career-high and franchise postseason-record 44 points, along with five rebounds and five assists, in a 115–107 loss to the Nuggets.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-62) In Game 4 of the [Western Conference Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_NBA_playoffs#(3)_Minnesota_Timberwolves_vs._(5)_Dallas_Mavericks "2024 NBA playoffs"), Edwards posted a near triple-double with 29 points, 10 rebounds and 9 assists in a 105–100 victory over the [Dallas Mavericks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas_Mavericks "Dallas Mavericks").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-63) Minnesota would go on to lose to Dallas in five games despite Edwards 28-point, 9-rebound and 6-assist outing in a 124–103 close-out loss in Game 5.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-64)

#### 2024–25 season: Three-point scoring leader

On January 4, 2025, Edwards scored a then career-high 53 points and tied his career-high with 10 three-pointers in a 119–105 loss to the [Detroit Pistons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detroit_Pistons "Detroit Pistons").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-65) On January 25, Edwards surpassed [Karl-Anthony Towns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl-Anthony_Towns "Karl-Anthony Towns") for the most career three-pointers in Timberwolves franchise history with 976, in a 133–104 win over the [Denver Nuggets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver_Nuggets "Denver Nuggets").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-66) On January 30, Edwards was named to his third [All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_NBA_All-Star_Game "2025 NBA All-Star Game") in a row as a Western Conference reserve.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-67) On February 5, Edwards recorded 49 points (20 in the third quarter) and 9 rebounds in a 127–109 win over the [Chicago Bulls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bulls "Chicago Bulls"). He tied [Kevin Garnett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Garnett "Kevin Garnett") for the second-most 30-point games and tied Karl-Anthony Towns for the most 40-point games in team history.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-68) The next day, Edwards had 41 points, seven rebounds and six assists in a 127–114 win over the [Houston Rockets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Houston_Rockets "Houston Rockets"). It was Edwards’ 14th career 40-point game, passing Towns (13) for the most in franchise history. He became just the third player in Minnesota history to tally back-to-back 40-point games, joining [Andrew Wiggins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Wiggins "Andrew Wiggins") (2017) and [Kevin Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Love "Kevin Love") (2014). He also broke the record for the youngest player in NBA history to reach 1,000 career three-point baskets (23y, 185d).[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-:0-69)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-71) On February 10, Edwards put up 44 points in a 128–107 loss to the [Cleveland Cavaliers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleveland_Cavaliers "Cleveland Cavaliers"). He became the first player in Timberwolves franchise history to achieve at least three consecutive 40-point games.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-72) On April 10, Edwards scored 44 points, including 18 during Minnesota's franchise-record, 52-point third quarter, and the Timberwolves beat the [Memphis Grizzlies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis_Grizzlies "Memphis Grizzlies") 141–125.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-73) At the end of the season, Edwards became the three-point scoring leader (320 3-pointers made). It was the first time in Edwards’ career that he reached 300 made 3s. It’s also the seventh-highest total in NBA history.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-74) He also finished third in the [NBA Clutch Player of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_Clutch_Player_of_the_Year "NBA Clutch Player of the Year") voting.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-75)

On April 27, in Game 4 of the first round of the playoffs, Edwards scored 43 points to go along with nine rebounds and six assists in a 116–113 win over the [Los Angeles Lakers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles_Lakers "Los Angeles Lakers").[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-76) On May 6, in Game 1 of the second round, Edwards recorded 23 points and a playoff career-high 14 rebounds in a 99–88 loss against the [Golden State Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_State_Warriors "Golden State Warriors").[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-77) On May 14, in Game 5, Edwards had 22 points, 7 rebounds, and a playoff career-high 12 assists in a 121–110 closeout victory over the Warriors, guiding the Timberwolves to their second consecutive [Western Conference Finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_NBA_playoffs#(1)_Oklahoma_City_Thunder_vs._(6)_Minnesota_Timberwolves "2025 NBA playoffs").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-78) On May 24, In Game 3 of the Western Conference Finals, Edwards tallied 30 points, nine rebounds and six assists in just three quarters, leading the Timberwolves to a 143–101 blowout win over the [Oklahoma City Thunder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oklahoma_City_Thunder "Oklahoma City Thunder"). The victory cut the Thunder’s series lead to 2–1 and marked the Timberwolves’ highest-scoring playoff game in franchise history.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-79) Minnesota went on to lose to Oklahoma City in five games.

#### 2025–26 season: All-Star Game MVP

On November 30, 2025, Edwards scored 32 points in a 125–112 win over the [San Antonio Spurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Antonio_Spurs "San Antonio Spurs"), marking his 102nd career 30-point game and setting a new Timberwolves franchise record.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-80)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-81) On December 2, Edwards scored a season-high 44 points to lead the Timberwolves to a 149–142 overtime victory over the [New Orleans Pelicans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_New_Orleans_Pelicans_season "2025–26 New Orleans Pelicans season"). He poured in 34 of those 44 points in the second half, including a driving layup with 2.3 seconds remaining in regulation that forced overtime.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-82)

On January 8, 2026, Edwards recorded 25 points, seven rebounds, and nine assists in a 131–122 win over the [Cleveland Cavaliers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_Cleveland_Cavaliers_season "2025–26 Cleveland Cavaliers season"). With the performance, he became the seventh player in NBA history to reach 10,000 career points before turning 25, joining [Kobe Bryant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kobe_Bryant "Kobe Bryant"), [Tracy McGrady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracy_McGrady "Tracy McGrady"), [LeBron James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LeBron_James "LeBron James"), [Carmelo Anthony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmelo_Anthony "Carmelo Anthony"), [Kevin Durant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Durant "Kevin Durant"), and [Luka Dončić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luka_Don%C4%8Di%C4%87 "Luka Dončić"). Edwards also became the third-youngest player in NBA history to reach 10,000 career points, trailing only LeBron James and Kevin Durant.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-83)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-84) On January 17, Edwards scored a career-high 55 points, including 26 in the fourth quarter, in a 126–123 loss to the [San Antonio Spurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_San_Antonio_Spurs_season "2025–26 San Antonio Spurs season").[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-85)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-86) On February 1, Edwards was named to his fourth [All-Star Game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_NBA_All-Star_Game "2026 NBA All-Star Game") in a row as a Western Conference reserve.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-87) He was named the [NBA All-Star Game MVP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBA_All-Star_Game_Most_Valuable_Player "NBA All-Star Game Most Valuable Player") after recording a total of 32 points and 9 rebounds in 26 minutes across 3 games for the USA Stars.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-88) On February 3, Edwards posted 41 points, six rebounds, six assists and five steals, while knocking down seven three-pointers, leading the Timberwolves to a 117–110 win over the [Memphis Grizzlies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis_Grizzlies "Memphis Grizzlies"). In doing so, he became the first player in franchise history to record at least 40 points, five steals and five made three-pointers in a single game.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-89)

On May 10, in Game 4 of the [Western Conference Semifinals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_NBA_playoffs#(2)_San_Antonio_Spurs_vs._(6)_Minnesota_Timberwolves "2026 NBA playoffs"), Edwards scored 36 points in a 114–109 victory over the [San Antonio Spurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_San_Antonio_Spurs_season "2025–26 San Antonio Spurs season") to tie the series at 2–2. In the process, Edwards recorded his 18th career playoff game with 30 or more points before turning 25, tying [Dwyane Wade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwyane_Wade "Dwyane Wade") for the fourth-most in NBA history. Ahead of him are LeBron James (30), Kobe Bryant (26), and Kevin Durant (22).[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-90) Minnesota went on to lose to San Antonio in six games.

## National team career

Edwards was a member of the [United States national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_men's_national_basketball_team "United States men's national basketball team") that competed in the [2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_United_States_FIBA_Basketball_World_Cup_team "2023 United States FIBA Basketball World Cup team"). He started all eight games and was selected in the [All-FIBA World Cup Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIBA_Basketball_World_Cup_All-Tournament_Team "FIBA Basketball World Cup All-Tournament Team"). He was the leading scorer for the U.S., averaging 18.9 points per game. The team finished in fourth place.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-91) He was named to the [2024 Olympic team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_men's_Olympic_basketball_team "2024 United States men's Olympic basketball team").[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-92) He helped Team USA win the gold medal, and in six games, he averaged 12.8 points, 2.8 rebounds, 1.2 assists and 1.3 steals per game while shooting 58% from the field.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-93)

## Player profile

Edwards plays primarily as a shooting guard. He is listed at 6 feet 4 inches (1.93 m) and weighs 225lb (102 kilograms).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Basketball-Reference.com-1) He’s known for his explosive athleticism, often going viral for his thunderous [poster dunks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posterized "Posterized"), including one over [John Collins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Collins_(basketball) "John Collins (basketball)") that the NBA named the 2023–24 Dunk of the Year.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-94)[The Ringer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ringer_(website) "The Ringer (website)") called him "a preposterous athlete with a nice jumper and better instincts".[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-95) He’s drawn comparisons to a young [Michael Jordan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jordan "Michael Jordan") for his ability to finish around the rim. “They have a lot of the same mannerisms. The moves, the fadeaway, the athleticism, the poster dunks… that same kind of work ethic, that same kind of ‘I don’t sleep at all at night because I’m ready to play, I’m ready to hoop,” according to teammate [Mike Conley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Conley_Jr. "Mike Conley Jr.").[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-96)

Despite pre-draft concerns that he was a limited long-range scorer, Edwards has developed an efficient, high-volume three-point shot — shooting 37% on eight attempts per game.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Basketball-Reference.com-1) He led the NBA in three-pointers made for the 2024–25 season.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-97) The same year, he became the youngest player in NBA history to make 1,000 threes.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-:0-69)

His stout frame, lateral speed and competitiveness have helped transform his reputation on the defensive end — [Team USA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_men's_national_basketball_team "United States men's national basketball team") coach [Steve Kerr](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Kerr "Steve Kerr") called his on-ball defense “amazing” during the FIBA World Cup.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-98) His ability to match up against both long wings and shifty guards has garnered praise from Timberwolves head coach [Chris Finch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Finch "Chris Finch"). Edwards himself believes his defense is “overlooked” by the national media.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-99) In 2024, he won the NBA Fan Favorite award for Block of Year after leaping to prevent a game-winning shot by the [Pacers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana_Pacers "Indiana Pacers")' [Aaron Nesmith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Nesmith "Aaron Nesmith").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-100)

## Personal life

Edwards's daughter, Aislynn, was born in March 2024.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-102) Edwards left the Timberwolves' March 1 game against the [Sacramento Kings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacramento_Kings "Sacramento Kings") at halftime to be with Aislynn's mother, Shannon Jackson, as their child was born.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-103) Edwards and Jackson got married on July 16, 2026.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-104)[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-105)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-106) Including Aislynn, Edwards reportedly has four children with four different women.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-107)

Edwards's mother, Yvette, and grandmother, Shirley, both died of cancer during an eight-month span in 2015, when he was in eighth grade. He has worn the No. 5 basketball jersey since high school to honor them, as they both died on the fifth day of the month.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-selfmade-108) After their deaths, Edwards was raised by his sister, Antoinette, and brother, Antoine, who shared [legal custody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Child_custody "Child custody") of him.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Towers-109) In high school, Edwards frequently worked as an instructor at youth camps.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-Pourtout-110) He intended to major in [marketing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marketing "Marketing") while attending the [University of Georgia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Georgia "University of Georgia").[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-bio-111)

During his childhood, Edwards also starred in baseball, often acting as his team's fourth or fifth hitter in the batting order. He has jokingly said he was very skilled at a variety of sports when he was younger. He owns two [dogs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dog "Dog") and has also expressed his affinity for [lions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lion "Lion"), although he does not believe he has the requisite space to care for one.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-112)

Edwards made his acting debut in the 2022 sports drama film _[Hustle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hustle\_(2022\_film) "Hustle (2022 film)")._[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-113)

In 2023, [Adidas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adidas "Adidas") released the AE1, his first signature shoe. It quickly became a best-seller, prompting the company to sign him to a multiyear extension worth "around $50 million".[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-114)

### Controversies

In September 2022, Edwards posted a video to his Instagram story referring to a group of shirtless men standing on a sidewalk with a homophobic slur.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-115) The NBA fined him $40,000 for using "offensive and derogatory language."[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-116)

In December 2023, Paige Jordae, an [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram") model, accused Edwards of impregnating her and then offering her $100,000 to get an abortion.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-117) Jordae posted screenshots of text messages with Edwards.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-118) The screenshots, which were initially posted to Jordae's Instagram story, also included a screenshot of a pending wire transfer of $100,000 on November 27, 2023.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-119) Edwards responded, "I am handling my personal matters privately and will not be commenting on them any further at this time."[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Edwards_(basketball)#cite_note-120)
